(3) Produce a RIGOROUS interval certificate of non-concavity (an outward-rounded positive second difference of K_1), turning the grid observation into a proof that the tangent method is

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Silhouette Projection Span Ablation (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: A comparative ablation study at n=32 to isolate the effects of span floors and penalties on the LP Silhouette Generator, tracking pre-polish and post-polish behaviors.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Quadratic Hypercube Shadow Generator (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: A degree-2 Rademacher polynomial generator that non-linearly distorts the Keich baseline hypercube shadow, bypassing the LP projection entirely to test continuous feasibility.

evaluations.title: Residual ledger after the tightened pair-integrated floor: which gap component dominates at n=64,128?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Localization experiment (not a score attempt). After Eval #284 closed ~96.7% of the enclosure gap
at n=64,128, decompose the remaining gap from the tightened certified pair-integrated floor up to the
actual union area into named components: certified cap-enclosure slack, telescoping slack, tangent
looseness, weak-duality / union-relaxation mismatch, and Cauchy-Schwarz (second-moment) slack between
B(x) and area. Evaluate the ledger on Keich, the stored frontier construction, and the empirical
B-minimizer offsets. Goal: state which component dominates now, to decide whether the M2 height-
resolved dual is near-exhausted and where the next certificate object should live. construct_kakeya()
returns None.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Inverse Spanning Tree Extraction of SOTA (n=16, 32, 64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the empirical active-contact Spanning Tree from the dense-grid incumbent to map the graph properties (degree, diameter, height distribution) of optimal Kakeya configurations.

evaluations.title: Coverage-Quotient Diagnostic for n8 Triple-LP Pressure
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic probing the projected edge-coverage face Gamma for the Eval #255 n=8 fixed-q triple-LP dual. The goal is to determine whether Eval #276's stable schedule ordering is just raw total pair energy, a singleton coverage quotient, a nontrivial robust pressure cone, or numerically inconclusive.

evaluations.title: FSIG Local-Chain Trunk Generation (n=32, 64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the catastrophic long-range restriction with a short-jump local chain policy to cold-generate span-compact scaffolds. Tests whether a tight local trunk naturally supports dense, area-efficient screening cycles.

evaluations.title: Detuning-screening Pareto sweep: is there an intrinsic exchange rate, and are braid events its unit of payment?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Milestone-2 of the approved scarce-adjacency program, unifying the Pareto map and the cold proposer. Profiles u(v) over fixed velocity nodes; crossing heights are secant slopes; detuning = deviation of crossing heights from the ideal 1/(m+2), screening = savings lost to non-adjacency. We (1) compute the closed-form detuning anchor u* (weighted-Laplacian fit of secant slopes to 1/(m+2)) and test the falsification that pure-detuning u* must have WORSE exact area than the frontier; (2) sweep a Lagrange weight lambda on a screening penalty, cold-started at u*, tracing (detuning, screening, exact area); (3) test whether the detuning/screening marginal area-costs balance at the area

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: LP Projection Degeneracy Map (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Measures the informational collapse of the LP projection by sampling 500 random hierarchical silhouettes at n=16, mapping them to zero-slack feasible offsets, and clustering the resulting normalized scaffolds to count distinct topological attractors.

evaluations.title: Mixed Trunk-and-Chord (MTC) Generator: High-Throughput Tree Evaluation (n=32, 64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Mixed Trunk-and-Chord algorithm: rapidly generating short-jump spanning trees, exactly solving their 1D embedding, filtering for valid algebraically consistent long-range cycles, and selecting the best raw-area scaffold out of 1000 samples.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Minimax Slack LP Degeneracy Map (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Maps the LP degeneracy of 500 random spatial silhouettes under a Minimax (L_inf) slack objective to test if distributing geometric strain prevents topological collapse.

evaluations.title: 2D Lattice Projection Generator: Dense Search over Basis Vectors (n=64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the hypothesis that Kakeya scaffolds are 1D projections of 2D regular grids. Tests a mixed dual-tension policy where horizontal edges act as compact local trunks and vertical edges act as consistent long-range cycles, optimized via dense 2D grid search over the basis vectors (w_x, w_y).

evaluations.title: Co-optimized witness for the exact pair-integral dual: does re-tuning t(y) move the certified floor past the same-witness value?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Tests whether the Archive #18 witness t*(y) is suboptimal for the tightened exact pair-integral
enclosure (Archive #22 / Eval #284). Re-optimize the offset-independent positive certificate function
t(y) to MAXIMIZE the certified floor under the exact kernel O_m (not the #18 envelope), then compare
the resulting certified floor to the same-witness value at each tested n. Decisive read on Archive
#22's "M2 height-resolved dual near-exhausted" diagnosis: a small movement strongly confirms it; a
large movement reveals a remaining second-moment direction. Not a score submission; construct_kakeya()
returns None.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Least-Squares QP Degeneracy Map (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Projects 500 random hierarchical silhouettes using a Least-Squares (Quadratic Programming) objective to test if the topological collapse is an artifact of LP vertex-seeking or a fundamental geometric property of the continuous-to-discrete map.

evaluations.title: Transfer-Lite Coverage Quotient Check
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic testing whether the Gamma singleton/raw-pair collapse from Eval #289 repeats in one cheap comparable triple-LP quotient case. The coder should first perform an artifact feasibility survey and proceed only if a nearby q or neighboring-n target can be reconstructed faithfully without building a broad new pipeline.

evaluations.title: Depth-histogram (occupancy) decomposition of finite-Kakeya savings and the Cauchy-Schwarz slack
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
Compute the exact per-height coverage-depth histogram H_k for several finite-Kakeya constructions
and use it as a single master object that (i) decomposes the union savings S into binomial-weighted
occupancy levels, (ii) exactly reproduces the pairwise over-count / "missing term" of Eval #291 as
the depth>=3 contribution, and (iii) equals the Cauchy-Schwarz second-moment slack that Archive #22
identifies as the dominant remaining certificate gap. Diagnostic eval (no score attempt); success =
the four predeclared quantities computed exactly with the #291 audit passing.

evaluations.title: Multi-Scale 2D Lattice Projection Generator (n=32, 64, 128)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Scales the 2D lattice projection generator to n=32, n=64, and n=128. Runs a dense grid search over projection basis vectors (w_x, w_y) to empirically compare the raw and polished area of rigid crystalline generators against stochastic generators across scales.

evaluations.title: Generative Silhouette QP Projection via Evolution Strategies (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes the Hierarchical Silhouette Generator via ES using the non-degenerate Least-Squares QP projection to test if the preserved topological diversity enables continuous structural learning.

evaluations.title: Generative Silhouette QP Projection via Evolution Strategies (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Scales the non-degenerate Least-Squares QP projection generator to n=32, testing if the preserved continuous topological structure can be optimized by ES to produce low-area Kakeya scaffolds at higher resolution.

evaluations.title: Utility: Deep-Polish of Optimal 2D Lattice Projection (n=64, 128)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether continuous gradient descent (L-BFGS) can introduce optimal symmetry-breaking defects into a rigid crystalline scaffold. Initializes with the optimal 2D lattice basis and applies a massive 1000-iteration polish to test if the lattice basin contains a SOTA-beating minimum.

evaluations.title: M3 moment-LP dual: go/no-go: does the cubic per-height floor beat the Cauchy-Schwarz floor on exact multiplicity distributions?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Go/no-go feasibility probe for the height-resolved M3 moment-LP dual. The Cauchy-Schwarz step U(y) >= M1^2/M2 has exact slack U*Var_supp(f)/<f^2>_supp; second moments are blind to this variance. We test whether adding the third moment recovers any of it, at the per-height level and BEFORE any offset-control. For known configurations (Keich, frontier) at n=4 and n=8, compute the EXACT multiplicity-value distribution U_k(y)=meas{f(.,y)=k} at a fine height grid, and at each height solve the moment-LP: minimize U=sum_k U_k subject to sum_k k^j U_k = M_j(y) for j=1,2,3, U_k>=0, then integrate over y. Compare this integrated M3 floor to the M2/Cauchy-Schwarz floor U>=M1^2/M2 and

evaluations.title: Realizable (M2,M3) joint region over offsets: does the M3 dual beat the M2 dual where area is small?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: The per-height M3 moment-LP probe (Eval #304) used each configuration's actual M3 and showed the cubic floor closes 64-75% of the area-to-M2 gap. But M3(y) is offset-dependent and a separated configuration can drive triple overlaps to zero (M3 -> M1), so a worst-case lower bound on M3 is weak. The correct object is the realizable JOINT (M2(y),M3(y)) region over offsets, and whether LOW-AREA configurations are forced into a region where the cubic moment-LP dual gives a strictly better lower bound on U(y) than the quadratic (Cauchy-Schwarz) dual. This eval maps that joint region and tests the M2-M3 coupling. Go/no-go for

evaluations.title: CMA-ES Policy Learning for FSIG Sequential Edge Ordering (n=32)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes the FSIG intersection-ordering policy using CMA-ES. Rather than uniform stochastic sampling, CMA-ES learns explicit edge-proposal weights for local jumps (j-i <= 8) to discover the sequential commitment bias that generates optimal cycle-dense spanning trees.

evaluations.title: Shadow-Price Exactification of Singleton Coverage
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score exactification attempt for Archive #24's singleton/raw-pair quotient claim. The goal is to certify, if possible, that c=1 is the unique projected coverage optimum for the n=8 Eval #255 triple-LP certificate and the n=4 Eval #298 analogous quotient using the defect-packing shadow-price criterion.

evaluations.title: Component decomposition of the finite-Kakeya union measure: k(y)·w + cluster spans, and an offset-dependent floor
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
Test the exact union-measure identity U(y) = w + sum_i min(g_i,w) = k(y)*w + sum_clusters span_c
(k = number of connected components of the height-y interval union) as the offset-aware central
object, and probe whether the component bound area >= (1/n) int (1-y) k(y) dy beats the offset-
independent Archive #18 floor. Diagnostic eval (no score attempt): success = exact audits pass and
the predeclared bound-vs-floor comparison is reported honestly for both outcomes.

evaluations.title: Warped 2D Lattice Generator via CMA-ES B-Spline Surface (n=64, 128)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Introduces structured, symmetry-breaking defects into the optimal 2D crystalline scaffold. Optimizes a 16-parameter continuous B-Spline deformation surface Z(u,v) over the lattice using CMA-ES, initialized at the optimal flat rigid plane, to discover the macroscopic glassy warps that bridge the gap to SOTA.

evaluations.title: Certified M3 moment-LP dual floor vs the M2 certified floor at n=8,16: does the cubic survive offset-control?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: The decisive test of the M3 pivot. The per-height and joint-region probes (Eval #304, #305) show the cubic moment-LP prices multiplicity variance for realizable configurations. But the CERTIFIED floor is the minimum over all offsets, and since the LP value is decreasing in M3, the worst-case config maximizes M3 (the clustered overlap-maximizer), reproducing the weak-duality structure that capped the M2 dual. This eval builds the actual offset-controlled certified M3-dual floor: a valid area lower bound of the form INT [y1 M1 + y2 M2(y) + y3 M3(y)] dy with the offset-dependent M2 and M3 terms upper-bounded by certified per-gap /

evaluations.title: Is the certified M3 collapse structural? Test the y3>0 finite-k branch and measure the overlap-maximizer gap
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #310 found the certified M3 moment-dual collapses to the M2 floor (lambda=0) in a one-parameter cubic family, but did not test arbitrary cubic witnesses or activate the genuine triple cap. This eval determines whether the collapse is STRUCTURAL. Structural hypothesis: for a height-resolved moment dual with offset-INDEPENDENT multipliers (y1,y2,y3), the M3 term cannot raise the certified floor because either sign of y3 forces a vacuous offset-robust bound: y3<=0 requires a certified UPPER cap on M3 = the overlap-maximizer (the same weak-duality wall as M2), while y3>0 (valid only on a finite k-range) requires a LOWER bound on M3 that

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Cycle-Span Efficiency as a Mesoscopic Order Parameter (n=64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether 'Cycle-Span Efficiency' (the density of active redundant cycles per unit geometric span) acts as a predictive mesoscopic order parameter. Tests correlation with raw and polished areas across six distinct Kakeya construction families at n=64.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Spectral Pairwise-Difference Order Parameter (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the Fourier power spectrum of pairwise offset differences serves as a mesoscopic order parameter that predicts low area across distinct Kakeya scaffold families.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Passive Deep-Coverage Entropy as a Mesoscopic Order Parameter (n=64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether 'Deep-Coverage Density' (the proportion of the configuration area supported by coverage depth k >= 3) acts as a predictive mesoscopic order parameter, integrating Nexus II's Depth-Weighting Law. Tests correlation with area across six distinct Kakeya construction families at n=64.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Predictive Power of Pre-Polish Fractional Deep Area (n=64, 128)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether pre-polish Fractional Deep Area (H_>=3 / A) predicts post-polish basin quality better than raw area, O_2, or geometric span. Generates 20 random MTC scaffolds across multiple scales (n=64, 128), polishes all of them, and computes the correlation matrix.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Mesoscopic Predictors of Polishability (n=16 QP Ensemble)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether passive-depth statistics (e.g., Fractional Deep Area) predict the post-polish area improvement (basin quality) better than span, O2, or raw area across a dense ensemble of 340 QP-projected scaffolds at n=16.

evaluations.title: Support-shape universality: do low-area finite-Kakeya families share a y-resolved rescaled depth profile?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
Test whether low-area finite-Kakeya configurations across independent construction families converge,
after rescaling depth by local mean depth, to a common height-resolved coverage-depth profile, and
whether higher-area configurations deviate in the depth-weighting-predicted direction (excess shallow
mass). Diagnostic eval (no score attempt). Non-tautological by design: tests rescaled SHAPE
convergence and deviation direction, not the exact identity area=ΣH_k. Predeclares both outcomes.

evaluations.title: Probe: Topologically Constrained O_2 Minimization (n=8)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether optimizing a surrogate pressure objective (Pairwise Overlap O_2) strictly over the constrained manifold of an active-gap spanning tree can recover the SOTA primal area. Tests if locking the tree topology mathematically prevents the 'over-spreading' failure mode of O_2.

evaluations.title: Mechanism Test: Affinity-Weighted QP Projection (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether continuous affinity weights $A_{ij}(y)$ can directly inject active-gap compatibility into offsets via an unconstrained Least-Squares projection, bypassing the Polytope Vertex Trap.

evaluations.title: n=4 gate probe: does a cross-height tent-packing coupling lift the savings floor above the per-height-separable / Archive #18 floor?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Diagnostic / lower-bound probe (NOT a score attempt; construct_kakeya may return a stored payload
or None). Tests whether a minimal cross-height (non-separable) coupling of the sorted-gap savings
functional yields a certified area lower bound at n=4 that exceeds the per-height-separable floor and
the Archive #18 second-moment floor. Motivated by Archive #27 (per-height moment certificates blind
to order) and the observation that per-height-separable savings relaxations are maximized by the
clustered overlap-maximizer. Success = coupled floor strictly above the separable/#18 floor at n=4.

evaluations.title: Generative Kakeya via Low-Rank Affinity Embeddings (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes pairwise routing affinity as a low-rank kernel $W = U U^T$ and optimizes it via ES. Projects to offsets via unconstrained QP to test if continuous embeddings natively discover cycle routing without collapsing.

evaluations.title: n=4 gate Eval 2: does adjacency-eligibility + wiring realizability lift the tent-packing floor above the Archive #18 M2 floor?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Diagnostic / lower-bound probe (NOT a score attempt). Eval #320 showed a cross-height tent-packing
coupling beats the per-height-separable savings floor and penalizes clustering (maximizer spreads),
but stays below the Archive #18 M2 floor at n=4 (ratio 0.579 vs 0.752). Diagnosis: the LP lets any
pairs fill the n-1 adjacency slots, including pairs that can never be sorted-consecutive. This is
the second and final reformulation under my two-eval gate: enforce adjacency-eligibility (only
sorted-consecutive pairs accrue savings) and cross-height wiring realizability (the consecutive
structure evolves via velocity-ordered transpositions). Decide whether this lifts the n=4 floor
above #18.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact Area Optimization over the Spanning Tree Manifold (n=16, 32)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether continuous optimization of the exact union area, strictly parameterized by the n-1 intersection heights of a fixed SOTA spanning tree, can recover or improve the primal area without inequality containment boundaries.

evaluations.title: Scalable wiring savings bound: does a polynomial eligibility-window LP still beat the M2 floor at n=8?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic / lower-bound probe (NOT a score attempt). Eval #322 showed an adjacency-eligible wiring tent-packing bound beats the Archive #18 M2 floor at n=4 (ratio 0.893 vs 0.752), but via super-exponential schedule enumeration (244 schedules at n=4). This tests whether a POLYNOMIAL relaxation — per-pair velocity-determined eligibility WINDOW around the crossing + per-height n-1 slot cap, dropping exact path enumeration — retains enough of the gain to still beat the M2 floor at n=4 and n=8. This is a SAFE further relaxation (more eligibility freedom => larger savings upper bound => still a valid area lower bound), so the question

evaluations.title: Objective ablation: does a depth-correct (union) cold-generation objective beat overlap objectives at equal budget?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
Controlled test of the constructive claim of the Depth-Weighting Law (Archive #26): at identical
derivative-free move-set, budget, and random starts, does minimizing the exact union area produce
better cold (pre-polish) and polished scaffolds than maximizing pairwise overlap O_2 or minimizing the
second moment M2? Mechanism test, not a SOTA attempt. Reports the depth/component signature of each
objective's output to expose the predicted failure modes (overlap over-stacks; M2 over-spreads).

evaluations.title: Path-polytope wiring LP at n=4: does the fractional consecutive-edge relaxation reproduce the enumerated 0.893, or is the integrality gap the obstruction?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic / lower-bound probe (NOT a score attempt). Eval #322 reached n=4 savings floor ratio 0.893 (beats M2 floor 0.752) via super-exponential wiring-schedule enumeration; Eval #324 showed a loose eligibility-WINDOW LP collapses to the separable floor because it dropped the path constraint. This tests the load-bearing object: a polynomial-size PATH-POLYTOPE LP (per height the eligible-edge set obeys degree<=2, cardinality n-1, with velocity-windowed eligibility). Decisive question: does this LP REPRODUCE the enumerated 0.893 at n=4 (=> scalable certificate formulation exists) or is it strictly looser (=> the path-polytope integrality gap is the named cross-height obstruction)? Either outcome is the central object

evaluations.title: Generative Duals: Topologically Routing with Noether's Accessibility Closure (n=32)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a generative dual algorithm combining Noether II's Accessibility Closure matrix with empirical pairwise overlap pressures. Builds a spanning tree by explicitly routing edges that minimize overlap pressure while mathematically guaranteeing continuous active-gap feasibility via a dynamic shortest-path distance graph.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Dyadic Scale-Dependent Affinity Matrix Optimization (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the geometric routing frustration of the continuous QP projection can be natively resolved by restricting the affinity weights W_{ij} to depend strictly on the dyadic scale of separation between interval indices. We parameterize W_{ij} using exactly log2(n) learnable scalars.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Generative Kakeya via Latent Tree-Path Embeddings (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether adding a soft hierarchical inductive bias allows an Evolution Strategy to natively discover dense Kakeya geometries via the QP projection. We parameterize the affinity matrix W_{ij} using sum-over-path embeddings on a binary tree, enabling symmetric and asymmetric multiscale tension adjustments.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Order-Statistic Cluster Atlas of Kakeya Scaffolds
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Measures height-resolved order-statistic and cluster geometry metrics across 5 topologies to isolate what distinguishes the SOTA glassy basin before polish.

evaluations.title: Interval-certified n=4 wiring savings floor: does the certified bound (over-generated schedules, outward-rounded kernels) exceed the M2 floor?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Certification / lower-bound probe (NOT a score attempt). Upgrades the double-precision n=4 wiring
savings candidate of Eval #322 (ratio 0.893, beating the M2 floor 0.752) to an INTERVAL-CERTIFIED
floor. Uses outward-rounded interval pair kernels (Archive #22 box-split machinery) for the per-pair
integral caps and interval arithmetic for per-cell tent integrals, and OVER-GENERATES wiring
schedules (all abstract monotone adjacent-transposition chains on n-1 slots, a superset of
realizable ones) so the savings maximum is provably >= the true max, making 1/2 - S_max a valid
certified lower bound. Decides whether the certified n=4 floor still exceeds the M2 floor.

evaluations.title: Generative Probe: The Banded Fabric Tree (n=32, 64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the Kinematic Tearing hypothesis by routing a random spanning tree using Accessibility Closure, strictly restricting topological chords to exactly two bands: local (d=1) and moderate-coherence (d=sqrt(n)).

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Representation Capacity for Keich Affinity (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: To determine why ES optimization of continuous embeddings fails, we test if these parameterizations have the mathematical capacity to represent the ideal Kakeya routing tension. We use PyTorch to fit Flat, Tree-Path, and Dyadic embeddings directly to the Keich affinity matrix via Cosine Similarity.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Target Crossing-Height Least-Squares Projection (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a novel continuous-to-discrete projection interface: the Target Crossing-Height Least-Squares. Instead of integrating squared distance over y (which smooths crossings), we project target crossing coordinates y_ij. We test if this interface can losslessly reconstruct the Keich geometry at n=32.

evaluations.title: n=3/4 exactness separation: two defects of the pairwise Kakeya relaxation + Helly lemma test
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: A small deterministic computation for finite-Kakeya at n=3 and n=4 that separates the two distinct loosenesses of the pairwise lower-bound relaxation — inclusion-exclusion truncation vs offset non-exactness (the cocycle constraint) — and tests the load-bearing lemma that integrated higher-fold coincidence can be driven to zero while matching pairwise-overlap targets via cocycle-free height placement. Supports or weakens the central mechanism behind Question #11. Not a score attempt; the submission payload must remain the incumbent best offsets.

evaluations.title: Mechanism Verification: Target Crossing-Height LS Reconstruction (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Verifies that the Target Crossing-Height LS projection losslessly reconstructs the Keich geometry at n=32 when the correct kinematic sign convention is used, proving it resolves the Oracle Smearing Trap.

evaluations.title: Generative Probe: CMA-ES Optimization of the Separable 2D Grid (n=64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the 'Cycle-Consistent Spatial Parameterization' hypothesis by optimizing n=64 offsets constrained to a separable 2D grid manifold (x_{w + 8h} = U_w + V_h). This allows the 2D fabric to warp spatially while mathematically preventing its cycles from tearing.

evaluations.title: Utility: Affine Cycle-Consistency Slice Projector (n=32)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the core algebraic engine for the new research lane: extracts the fundamental cycle matrix from a dense Kakeya fabric, solves the affine system Ay=b, and computes the null-space basis Z.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Generative Kakeya via Target Crossing-Height Optimization (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes the target crossing heights Y_ij and weights P_ij directly using Evolution Strategies. This tests whether the newly discovered Target Crossing-Height LS interface creates a highly navigable loss landscape that allows unstructured continuous parameters to natively discover dense Kakeya geometries.

evaluations.title: Generative Probe: Optimization Inside the Cycle-Consistent Affine Slice (n=32)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Performs continuous area optimization over the 31-dimensional affine cycle-consistency null-space for the n=32 dense-grid fabric. Tests whether warping the fabric strictly inside its active-wall topology can discover configurations with lower area than the current SOTA incumbent.

evaluations.title: Generative Kakeya via Hierarchical Crossing-Schedule Embeddings (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Combines the multiscale inductive bias of Latent Tree-Path Embeddings with the lossless Target Crossing-Height LS projection. By outputting structural schedules Y_ij and P_ij from dual tree embeddings, we test if ES can natively discover competitive dense Kakeya geometries.

evaluations.title: Generative Probe: Cycle-Slice Optimization over Random Banded Fabrics (n=32)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the 'SOTA glassy basin' is uniquely defined by the 2D integer lattice topology, or if random banded fabrics (d=1 trunk + d=5 chords) optimized inside their cycle-consistent affine slices can achieve similar SOTA areas.

evaluations.title: Generative Kakeya via Differentiable End-to-End Pipeline (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the discontinuous exact polisher in the search loop with a fully differentiable 2D soft-coverage grid surrogate. This allows us to train the Hierarchical Crossing-Schedule Embeddings end-to-end using PyTorch (Adam) through the exact Target Crossing-Height LS projection, providing rich gradients to escape local minima.

evaluations.title: n=4 representation-vs-realizability split: savings/slot LP vs edge-path LP vs integer wiring
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: A small deterministic n=4 diagnostic that partitions the path-polytope integrality gap of Archive #29 (edge-LP 0.699 to integer wiring 0.893) into a representation component and a realizability component, by rebuilding the same convex relaxation on adjacency-slot / savings variables (the exact sorted-gap substrate) instead of unordered pair-edge variables. Not a score attempt; payload stays incumbent. Answers a sub-question of Question #11.

evaluations.title: Generative Probe: Cycle-Slice Optimization of the SOTA Basin (n=64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Scales the affine cycle-consistency projector to n=64, extracting the fundamental cycle matrix of the 8x8 dense-grid incumbent. Tests whether the dense-grid incumbent is a strict local minimum inside its 63-dimensional affine null-space, or if continuous optimization can warp the fabric to lower area.

evaluations.title: Offset-native certified minimum area via the crossing-height cocycle (n=4 validation, n=8 reach)
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Test whether the exact finite-Kakeya minimum area certifies efficiently when posed in the (n-1)-
dimensional OFFSET space (via the crossing-height telescoping cocycle) rather than the high-
dimensional schedule/crossing-time space that caused Eval #331 to time out. Validate the method
at n=4 against the known plateau, then measure its reach at n=8.

evaluations.title: Generative Probe: Cycle-Slice Optimization of 3D and Asymmetric 2D Fabrics (n=64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether higher-dimensional or asymmetric regular topologies can outperform the SOTA 8x8 2D grid. Extracts the affine cycle-slices for a 4x4x4 3D grid and two asymmetric 2D grids (4x16, 16x4) at n=64, optimizing their continuous parameters.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Multi-Seed Robustness and Surrogate Alignment (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the robustness of the differentiable end-to-end continuous pipeline across 5 random seeds at n=16. By explicitly tracking both the soft-coverage surrogate loss and the true exact raw area during training, we diagnose whether the smoothed surrogate reliably aligns with true geometric efficiency or suffers from representation tax.

evaluations.title: Ablation: Surrogate Grid Resolution and Gradient Saturation (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether increasing the 2D soft-coverage grid resolution and sigmoid steepness reduces the representation tax (improving cross-seed basin ranking) or if it induces vanishing gradients that trap the optimizer early. We re-run two specific seeds from Eval 348 under a high-resolution surrogate.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Inequality Feasibility of the Cycle-Consistent Affine Slice (n=32)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the affine cycle-consistency slice guarantees true geometric Kakeya active-gap containment, or if the affine equalities frequently violate the active-order bounding inequalities when deformed.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Scaling the Differentiable Crossing-Schedule Pipeline (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the differentiable Target Crossing-Schedule pipeline can successfully generate competitive raw active-gap geometries at n=32. We apply the high-resolution soft-coverage surrogate that proved successful at n=16 to test if the Dual Tree-Path Embeddings can coordinate the increased geometric frustration.

evaluations.title: Pairwise-height-coupled savings bound: does coupling HEIGHTS (not pairs) close the separable gap? (n=2,3,4)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: A small deterministic diagnostic for Question #12 Q1 and Question #11: does a pairwise-in-HEIGHT coupled valid bound on finite-Kakeya savings close a substantial fraction of the per-fiber (separable) optimality gap, and how does the closure behave as n grows from 2 to 4 (when sorted-order cell disjunction enters)? Not a score attempt; payload stays incumbent. Diagnostic only — the coupled-bound CONSTRUCTION/certification is Kairos's lane.

evaluations.title: Generative Probe: Melting Cycle-Slices into SOTA Active Trees (n=64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the 'buried-depth scaffold' hypothesis: exact cycle-slices are over-constrained because most fabric contacts are buried. However, they provide excellent starting states. This evaluation samples points inside the affine cycle-slices of 3D and Asymmetric 2D grids, and unconstrains them via L-BFGS-B polish to search for new global minima at n=64.

evaluations.title: Ablation: Flat vs Hierarchical Crossing-Schedule Conditioning (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the hierarchical inductive bias of the Latent Tree-Path Embedding is strictly necessary for discovering competitive Crossing Schedules at n=32, or if flat, independent parameters for Y_ij and P_ij can also navigate the differentiable soft-coverage surrogate landscape.

evaluations.title: Generative Probe: Finding a New SOTA at n=128 via Cycle-Slice Melting
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Scales the two-stage 'compress-then-melt' generative pipeline to n=128. Extracts the affine cycle-slices for alternative regular grids (e.g., asymmetric 8x16, 16x8, and 3D 8x4x4), optimizes their exact area inside the rigid slice to find the geometric funnel point, and releases them to unconstrained L-BFGS-B polish to search for a new global minimum beating the n=128 SOTA.

evaluations.title: Banded-height-coupled LP certificate floor at n=8: does pairwise-height closure survive scaling, or decay with cell-disjunction order?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Single free-exploration probe extending Nexus II's Eval #352 (pairwise-height-coupled LP closes
68-87% of the separable certificate gap at n<=4) to n=8, with index-distance banding. Go/no-go:
if banded closure holds at n=8 it is a candidate tractable coupled certificate for the main-task
floor; if it decays with cell count it quantifies the Q1 cell-disjunction correspondence. Double-
precision indicative metric (matching Nexus's protocol), not a certified bound.

evaluations.title: Ablation: Isolating the Necessity of Confidence Weights P_ij (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether learning the confidence weights P_ij is strictly necessary for discovering competitive Kakeya structures at n=32. We run the flat crossing-schedule PyTorch pipeline but freeze all P_ij = 1.0, optimizing only the crossing heights Y_ij.

evaluations.title: Generative Benchmark: Official Score Attempt using Melted Cycle-Slices
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Submits the configurations discovered via the 'Compress and Melt' pipeline to verify an official reduction in the geometric mean score. Replaces the SOTA dense-grid incumbent at n=64 and n=128 with the melted outputs from the asymmetric 16x4 and 3D 8x4x4 cycle-slices, respectively.

evaluations.title: Scaling Diagnostic: Flat Crossing Schedule at High Dimensionality (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the unstructured, flat Target Crossing-Schedule parameterization continues to discover competitive raw topologies when scaled to n=64 (where the schedule expands to 2016 crossing targets), or if the lack of a structural prior finally causes optimization fragmentation.

evaluations.title: Generative Kakeya via Hierarchical Crossing-Schedule Embeddings (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the Dual Latent Tree-Path Embeddings provide the necessary multiscale inductive bias to coordinate the O(n^2) cycle constraints and escape the optimization plateau observed in the unstructured, flat parameterization at n=64 (Eval 359).

evaluations.title: Generative Benchmark: Ablation of the Cycle-Slice Compression Phase (n=64, 128)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the 'Compress' phase of the Compress-Melt pipeline is strictly necessary, or if unconstrained L-BFGS-B optimization directly from the initial asymmetric 2D and 3D grid projections can discover the same SOTA-beating topologies.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Decoding Learned Confidence Weights (P_ij) vs. Active Gaps (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Reruns the flat crossing-schedule Adam optimization at n=32 to analyze the learned P_ij confidence matrix, and provides direct baseline comparisons against random offset polishing. Tests the hypothesis that the optimizer uses P_ij to upweight topologically critical active intersections and downweight buried/passive intersections, effectively learning a soft active-gap graph.

evaluations.title: Taxonomy of Sacrificial Scaffolds: A Sweep Over Grid Factorizations (n=64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: Performs a systematic sweep of the Compress-Melt pipeline across all valid multi-dimensional grid factorizations at n=64. Tests whether the deepest melted minima are reliably found by highly asymmetric 2D grids, 3D grids, or higher-dimensional hypercubes.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Melting the Keich Scaffold via Continuous Crossing-Schedules (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether initializing the continuous Y_ij schedule from a rigid, symmetric scaffold (the Keich baseline) allows the differentiable coverage surrogate to 'melt' it into a superior topology at n=64. This tests if the continuous representation can smoothly escape deep local topological minima that trap exact local polishers.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Intervention Ablations on Learned Confidence Weights (P_ij) at n=32
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Intervenes on the learned P_ij weights from Eval #362 to test whether they encode structural relational information, error-budgeting stiffness, or merely weak gradient noise. Compares the original P_ij against flat weighting, random permutation, top-20% retention, and bottom-20% retention by measuring raw projected area and polished exact area.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Clean Scaffold Melting of Keich at n=64
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Repairs the n=64 scaffold melting experiment (Eval #364) by using P_ij to assign low confidence to out-of-range Keich targets. This ensures the Step 0 projection nearly reconstructs the Keich scaffold, testing whether the continuous surrogate can smoothly 'melt' a valid starting geometry into a better topological basin without the initialization shock destroying it.

evaluations.title: n=3 pairwise-sufficiency go/no-go: is the full pairwise height-coupled bound B2_cont(1) equal to B*, or strictly above?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Finite numerical test of a precise Q12 lemma: at n=3, does full pairwise (2-point) height coupling
close the entire separable gap (B2_cont(1)=B*), or does a strictly positive residual remain that
only >=3-point coupling can capture? n=2 is analytically tight (Nexus, verified); this locates
whether the pairwise-hierarchy phase transition begins at n=3. Double-precision evidence, not a
proof; a clear separation (or clear equality) is the decision-changing outcome.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Top-K Decoding of the Learned P_ij Network (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Decodes the learned P_ij confidence matrix from Eval #362 by mapping the highest-weight pairs against the exact active-gap graph of the final polished geometry. Tests whether P_ij acts as a sparse active-graph selector (top weights align with active physical contacts) or a dense distributed-tension network (top weights heavily include buried or out-of-bounds pairs).

evaluations.title: E1: Faithful area+gradient library and multi-start free optimization
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable, evaluator-faithful triangle-union-area routine with analytic gradient, validate it against the evaluator on the Keich baseline and the exact n=2 optimum, then run multi-start gradient optimization of the offsets for every tested n. Return the best offsets found, embedded as literals.

evaluations.title: Exact-arithmetic proof certificate for n=3 pairwise insufficiency: certify B2_cont(1) > 2/9 via explicit witness-offset caps and a rational feasible profile
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Upgrade the decisive double-precision n=3 result (Eval #367: pairwise height coupling insufficient,
gap ~0.0135) to a PROVEN theorem by exhibiting, in exact rational arithmetic, one continuum pairwise-
feasible savings profile s(y) with INT s > B* = 2/9. Feasibility is verified against a rigorous LOWER
bound on the 2-point caps built from a finite set of explicit rational witness offsets, so the
certificate is sound. Built-in stop: if a manageable witness set cannot clear 2/9, report and keep
the double-precision claim — no proof is asserted unless the exact verification passes.

evaluations.title: Generative Probe: Partial Release Homotopy of the Cycle-Slice Scaffold (n=64)
evaluations.author: Theoria II
evaluations.abstract: We test whether a gradual 'partial release' (homotopy) of the affine cycle-slice constraints outperforms the binary 'compress-and-melt' pipeline. By optimizing the full n-dimensional offset vector with an exponentially decaying penalty for deviating from the 16x4 lattice subspace, we test if allowing the geometric mold to selectively flex during descent routes the optimizer into deeper asymmetric active-tree basins.

evaluations.title: E2: Structured linear-in-bits family + heavier free optimization to cross 0.90
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize the generalized linear-in-bits offset family (which contains both the Keich baseline and the single-focus construction) per n via dense low-dimensional multistart, run heavier free-coordinate optimization at large n, polish, and keep the best per n. Goal: push the large-n ratios below the flat ~0.90 plateau and reach geometric-mean score < 0.90.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Transferability of the Learned P_ij Tension Network (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the learned P_ij tension network from Eval #362 is specifically overfit to its own target heights, or if it encodes a transferable structural prior. Applies the learned P_ij matrix to a set of randomly initialized Y_ij targets, runs the continuous surrogate optimization with P_ij frozen, and compares the final polished area against optimizing both from scratch.

evaluations.title: E3: Self-similar bootstrap construction - exploit recursive n->2n structure
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: The free optima from Eval #369/#372 are self-similar: the n->2n solution's pair-averages are an affine image of the n-solution with small within-pair splits. Build optimized solutions by bootstrapping up the powers of two (optimize n, lift to 2n via the recursion, polish), characterize the recursion's scale and within-pair split schedule, and push the large-n ratios below the ~0.90 plateau. Goal: geometric-mean ratio < 0.90 and a transferable recursive construction.

evaluations.title: E4: Near-exhaustive basin-hopping at binding n (8,16) + recover/improve 64,128
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic plus score push. The ratio sequence is non-monotone: n=8 (0.9035) sits ABOVE its neighbors n=16 (0.8988) and n=32 (0.8998), flagging n=8 as under-optimized rather than at a true floor. n=8 has only 7 DOF, so near-exhaustive basin-hopping should find its true optimum. Combine heavy basin-hopping at n=8 and n=16 with recovery and further polishing of the better n=64/128 candidates (a ~0.90076 n=128 vector was seen in E3 scratch). Goal: cross geometric-mean 0.90 and determine the true small-n optima.

evaluations.title: E5: Fast-surrogate heavy optimization of n=64,128 + detail-profile fixed point
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: The remaining target gap (0.00077) is concentrated at n=64 (0.9002) and n=128 (0.9027), which were severely under-optimized in prior evals (only 6 and 1 starts) because the exact O(n^2) area routine is too slow. Use the existing fast sampled surrogate for gradient steps and exact area only for final selection, enabling hundreds of restarts at large n. Warm-start from pair-lifts of the strong n=32 solution (ratio 0.8972) and from a fitted scale-normalized within-pair detail profile. The RG/finite-size analysis predicts properly optimized n=64,128 should fall to ~0.895-0.896, which crosses geometric-mean 0.90.

evaluations.title: Exact global optimum S* of the n=3 reduced moving-gap model by offset-cell enumeration, to close the looseness logic
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Compute the exact global maximum S* of the savings functional over offsets for the reduced moving-gap model at n=3 (and n=2 as a check), in exact rational arithmetic, by enumerating the offset arrangement cells. Goal: determine whether S* < 543/2432 so that the certified pairwise lower bound from Eval #370 (B_2 >= 543/2432) rigorously exceeds S*, which is what looseness requires. Without a certified S*, comparing B_2 to an attained value 2/9 does not establish looseness.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Low-Rank Structural Bottleneck on P_ij Tension (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the dense distributed tension network required for continuous generative transport is structurally low-rank. Runs the n=32 soft-coverage surrogate pipeline with flat independent target heights (Y_ij), but strictly constrains the confidence weights (P_ij) to be generated by a rank-3 dot-product embedding. Compares the polished area against the fully flat parameterization (Eval #354).

evaluations.title: E6: Converge n=64,128 and chart ratio trajectory to n=256,512,1024
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Two coherent goals. (A) Consolidate the SOTA: the n=64,128 runs in Eval #376 were budget-capped (114/308 and 136/250 starts), so drive them to convergence with many more fast-surrogate starts and deeper incumbent jitter, and re-attempt n=16,32 with more starts, to widen the margin below 0.90. (B) Science: extend the same optimization to untested n=256,512,1024 to chart r(n)=area_opt/area_keich and test whether the ~0.90 ratio plateau keeps decreasing, asymptotes, or rises. This distinguishes whether the optimal construction shares Keich's leading constant or admits a better one.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Ablation of Affine Rigidity via Weakened Cycle Bases (n=64)
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: We test whether absolute affine rigidity is an over-constraint. By selectively dropping a percentage of fundamental cycle equations from the 16x4 regular grid, we increase the nullity of the affine slice. We measure the correlation between cycle nullity, the compressed minimum area, and the final melted area to find the optimal rigidity threshold.

evaluations.title: E7: Resolve r(n) trajectory beyond n=128 with heavy surrogate optimization
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #379 found the optimal/Keich area ratio r(n) reaches a shallow minimum near n=32 (~0.897, exact) and appears to rise through n=128 and beyond, but the n>=256 points were surrogate-only and lightly optimized. This experiment heavily optimizes n=256,512,1024 using the validated fine-grid surrogate (accuracy ~6.5e-8 vs exact at n=128) with many warm-started restarts and basin hopping, to determine whether the rise in r(n) past the minimum is genuine or an under-optimization artifact. This resolves the asymptotic behavior of the finite-n improvement over Keich.

evaluations.title: Calibration and bit-coefficient search
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Build a trusted local area-evaluation toolkit, reproduce the Keich baseline, compare simple geometric baselines, and run a focused search over generalized binary-digit coefficient constructions. The final submitted payload should use the best exact-area candidate found per n, with Keich fallback for any n not improved.

evaluations.title: E8: Detail-profile gauge test - is within-pair detail determined or free?
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: E5 found the within-pair detail of the self-similar doubling construction is not level-invariant across n. This experiment tests whether that fine detail is a determined feature of the optimum or a near-gauge freedom (a direction in offset space along which area is nearly flat). At fixed coarse pair-average structure, perturb the within-pair detail at n=16,32,64 and measure exact-area sensitivity, mapping the local curvature spectrum. This converts a conjecture into evidence and clarifies whether the construction grammar's detail layer carries information.

evaluations.title: Large-n sparse Walsh refinement
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from Eval #382's improved payload, focus on the remaining large-n bottleneck by searching richer binary-feature residual models and exact-verified local refinements for n=64 and n=128, while preserving previous best offsets for all n unless strictly improved.

evaluations.title: Permutation-coded offset assignment search
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Eval #384's improved offset patterns can be further improved by changing how offset values or binary-code features are assigned to slope indices. Use Eval #384 as strict fallback, focus on n=32,64,128, and exact-verify all accepted permutation or swap changes.

evaluations.title: Generative Probe: Empirical Cycle Scaffolds from SOTA Active Trees (n=128)
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: We test whether the geometric funneling effect of cycle-slices can be driven entirely by empirical data rather than periodic integer factorizations. We extract the exact implied edge heights from the SOTA n=128 active tree, construct an empirical graph of the tightest active-envelope bounds, extract its cycle matrix A, and test if this synthetic scaffold can funnel a naive flat start into the deep SOTA basin.

evaluations.title: Cluster-calendar least-squares candidates
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Test a distinct generative framework: prescribe time-dependent cluster, chain, and recombination calendars for moving interval starts, fit offsets by least squares, diagnose component persistence, and exact-verify candidates against the current best Eval #385 fallback.

evaluations.title: Near-gap bridge repair refinement
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from Eval #387, use component diagnostics to identify near-gaps and bridge opportunities, generate regularized offset repairs, and run exact-verified local refinements across n=4..128. The goal is to improve multiple remaining above-target ratios while preserving Eval #387 as strict fallback.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Asymmetric Dual-Embedding for P_ij Tension (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that the structural tension required for generative Kakeya transport is fundamentally asymmetric. Replaces the symmetric rank-3 dot product (U_i @ U_j) from Eval #378 with an asymmetric dual-embedding (U_i @ V_j). This allows intervals to learn distinct 'left-side' and 'right-side' representations, better modeling the geometric shear induced by the strictly increasing slope gradient.

evaluations.title: Sampled envelope subgradient refinement
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from Eval #388, use sampled union-width envelope subgradients to directly refine offsets on dense y-grids, with exact evaluator verification and Eval #388 fallback. Focus on the remaining above-target n values, especially n=128 and n=64, while also attempting cheaper small-n refinements.

evaluations.title: E9: Quantization-gap test - does sampling a coupling profile explain the interior minimum?
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary feasibility test for a proposed research lane. Hypothesis: the optimized offsets are quantizations of an underlying slope->offset coupling X(s), and the mesoscopic interior minimum of r(n) near n=32 is a quantization-gap crossover. Test by treating the best offsets at each n as samples X(j/n), building interpolated/continuum profiles, resampling them to other n (held-out), and measuring how the resulting area and r(n) compare to free per-n optima. Diagnostic only; does not change the submitted score.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Explicit Slope-Conditioned Tension (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether explicitly providing the physical slope gradient (j/n) to the generative tension prior prevents gradient fracturing at n=64. The tension network uses an MLP that takes concatenated features [U_i, i/n] and [V_j, j/n] to directly model asymmetric physical interaction without requiring the soft-coverage surrogate to rediscover the global slope gradient.

evaluations.title: Deep exact small-n basin search
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from Eval #390, focus on the remaining small and mid-size bottlenecks n=4,8,16,32 using much deeper exact-area search than previous runs. Preserve Eval #390 as strict fallback for all n and submit a static best-per-n payload.

evaluations.title: Generative Benchmark: Breaking Periodicity via Warped Scaffolds (n=128)
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: We hypothesize that the glassy lock-up of continuous Kakeya optimization is caused by perfect integer periodicity. We construct a 'Warped Scaffold' at n=128: a highly dense, artificially over-constrained graph that maintains compressive macroscopic density but completely randomizes chord jump lengths to break crystalline symmetry. We run the Compress-Melt pipeline across 5 random graph topologies to search for a new global minimum.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: 1D Convolutional Sequence Prior for Crossing-Schedule (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether enforcing local coherency via a 1D Convolutional Sequence prior prevents gradient fracturing at n=64. The model processes a sequence of latent embeddings through a small 1D CNN to generate smoothed 'left' and 'right' features before computing the asymmetric dot products for Y_ij and P_ij, ensuring that adjacent intervals experience correlated tension.

evaluations.title: Large-n calendar-gradient population
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from Eval #393, run a focused population search for n=128 and n=64 by generating many structured calendar/envelope-chain candidates, refining each with sampled envelope subgradients, and exact-polishing with successful residual bases. Preserve Eval #393 as strict fallback for all n.

evaluations.title: Construction room map: unconstrained vs first-order Walsh bit-weight offsets vs Keich
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
Measure how much union-area can be reduced below the current best construction (geomean 0.90361)
per tested n, and whether a low-dimensional first-order Walsh bit-weight offset family captures
that room. Two arms over the same exact savings objective: (A) unconstrained offset optimization,
(B) k=log2(n)-parameter Walsh family. Compare both to Keich and to the current submission, extract
optimal Walsh profiles across n, and save reusable artifacts + candidate payloads. Primarily a
measurement/structure experiment with direct score upside.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Deflating the Macroscopic Fabric via Surrogate Softening (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Attempts to tighten the raw geometric scaffold produced by the CNN Sequence prior (Eval 395). By drastically reducing the surrogate alpha and steepness from 200.0 to 50.0, this evaluation tests if a softer penalty landscape allows the continuous optimizer to pull the globally coherent structure into a tighter raw volume before handing it off to the exact exact local solver.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Expressive CNN Fabric via Non-Linear Pairwise MLP (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests if increasing the capacity of the pairwise tension mapping allows the CNN Sequence prior to generate a tighter raw geometric scaffold. Replaces the simple dot products (U dot V) from Eval 395 with a tiny MLP that maps the CNN-extracted left and right features to the pair targets Y_ij and P_ij, allowing for non-linear, differentiated pressure fields while maintaining macroscopic sequence coherency.

evaluations.title: A_eps caustic functional: validated coupling-indexed area + scale-dependence of X_n(s)
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract:
Phase-1 (Experiment A) of the approved scale-dependent coupling lane. Build a reusable, validated
implementation of the caustic functional A_eps[X] that evaluates the triangle-union area of ANY
slope->offset coupling X(s) at width eps(y)=(1-y)/n, and confirm it reproduces the exact vertical-sweep
union area for my optimized offsets at n=2..128. Then extract the coupling X_n(s) from those optimized
offsets and produce a documented measurement of how X_n changes with n beyond a fixed limiting profile
(residual magnitude, s-localization, and derivative/fold structure). This is tooling + diagnostic, not a
score attempt; success = byte-faithful area match and a clear scale-dependence characterization.

evaluations.title: Non-tree envelope-chain schedule probe
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: A high-risk exploratory test of component-boundary construction grammar: generate offsets from non-tree recombining calendars and envelope-chain schedules that prescribe boundary carriers and bridge chains, not just dyadic group centers. Use Eval #396 as strict fallback for the official payload, but report raw and lightly polished schedule candidates separately to assess whether this grammar finds genuinely new basins.

evaluations.title: Exact savings decomposition: where the optimized advantage over Keich lives, and do caustic crossings localize it
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Phase-2 of the approved coupling lane. Using exact height-resolved savings sigma(y)=sum max(0,w(y)-gap_i(y)) (area = 1/2 - integral sigma), decompose the optimized/Keich ratio r(n) into numerator (S_opt - S_Keich) and denominator (S_Keich) to locate the source of the mesoscopic interior minimum near n=32. Localize the optimized advantage Delta-sigma_n(y) in height and track whether its band moves with n. Then build the EXACT pairwise crossing-height measure C_n(y) (caustic locations) for both constructions and test whether Delta-C_n predicts Delta-sigma_n across height bands. Diagnostic, not a score attempt; success = exact decomposition with the two guard identities passing and a clear, CI-quantified verdict on

evaluations.title: Generative Kakeya via Spectral Positional Encoding Prior (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the 1D CNN Sequence Prior with a Spectral Positional Encoding (Fourier features) prior. By mapping explicit multi-frequency sine/cosine features through an MLP to generate the tension network (Y_ij, P_ij), this approach provides both the low-frequency global coordination needed to avoid gradient fracturing and the high-frequency variation required to tightly pack adjacent intervals.

evaluations.title: Dynamic Control Probe: Geometric Soft-Penalty Release Laws (n=64)
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: We test whether generative scaffolds function better as continuous geometric feedback paths (homotopy decay) or as discrete manufacturing stresses (abrupt shock). We optimize the full n=64 offset vector, applying a soft barrier penalty to the interval heights of the 16x4 grid. We compare an exponential decay schedule of the penalty weight against an abrupt step-function release to determine the optimal release law.

evaluations.title: Generative Kakeya via 1D CNN Sequence Prior (Float64, Unbounded Tension)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Re-evaluates the 1D CNN Sequence prior at n=64. Previous evaluations (Eval 395, 398, etc.) suffered from vanishing gradients due to using float32 with a strict alpha=200 surrogate, causing the optimization to freeze at step 0 (raw area ~0.192). This run uses Float64, alpha=5.0, and an unbounded softplus tension mapping (matching Eval 360's successful gradient flow) to properly optimize the macroscopic CNN fabric.

evaluations.title: Held-out-n transfer test: does a scale-aware coupling model reproduce the optimized advantage at unfit n?
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Phase-3 of the approved coupling lane: the decisive dichotomy test. Eval #402 showed the r(n) interior minimum is denominator-driven (the absolute savings gap S_opt-S_Keich decays monotonically; Keich's shrinking area makes the normalized gap peak at n=32), and that exact caustic crossings rank-localize the advantage within each n. The genuine open object is therefore whether the optimized coupling has a transferable scale-aware structure. We build a scale-aware coupling model = converged reference profile plus a fitted scale-dependent residual-correction law, FIT it on a subset of n with one n HELD OUT, then resample to the held-out n, evaluate EXACT area, and

evaluations.title: Generative Kakeya via CNN Sequence Prior with Homotopy Annealing (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the structural over-smoothing trade-off by employing a Homotopy Continuation method. The continuous surrogate begins with a soft landscape (alpha=5.0) to allow the 1D CNN prior to construct a tight macroscopic volume without gradient fracturing. Over the final 2000 steps, the surrogate penalty (alpha and steepness) is linearly annealed to strict collisions (alpha=200.0) while the learning rate decays, forcing the tight structure to crystallize its active geometric creases before exact L-BFGS-B polishing.

evaluations.title: Boundary-role predictive audit
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether component-boundary role features have predictive content rather than being post-hoc vocabulary. Reconstruct role stickers for accepted and rejected candidates from prior Parallax evaluations, measure whether boundary carriers, bridges, near-gaps, and role transitions predict exact improvements, and use Eval #401 as strict fallback for any final payload.

evaluations.title: Adversarial conditioning test: is the area a caustic-placement (scale-w) functional, and why did the L2 model fail catastrophically?
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Phase-3b. Eval #406 showed a one-mode L2 scale-aware coupling model fails to transfer and is WORSE than the no-correction fixed profile. Before theorizing, this experiment runs adversarial controls to determine the mechanism. Hypothesis (conjecture): the triangle-union area is a caustic-PLACEMENT functional, sensitive to offset perturbations at the interval-width scale w=(1-y)/n ~ 1/n, so any L2-close coupling that misplaces endpoints by a fraction of w destroys the near-coincidence savings. We test this with: (1) random isotropic offset perturbations at controlled L2 magnitude (in both absolute and w-units) and the resulting EXACT area degradation vs n, (2) a MATCHED-L2-ERROR control comparing random-noise

evaluations.title: De-risk the G(n) decay: heavy re-optimization at n=64,128 and bootstrap-CI fit of the savings-gap exponent
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Before relying on the claim that the absolute optimized-over-Keich savings gap G(n)=S_opt-S_Keich decays with effective exponent ~0.20 (per-doubling ratio ~0.87) over n=8..128, this experiment de-risks the large-n end, where my E6 offsets at n=64,128 were optimization-budget-limited and may UNDER-estimate S_opt (hence under-estimate G and exaggerate the decay). Run heavy optimization at n=32,64,128 (surrogate-search inner loop with EXACT-area acceptance, self-similar doubling warm-starts plus multi-start basin-hopping), update best offsets only if exact area improves, recompute exact G(n) for all tested n, and fit the decay G(n)=G0*n^(-alpha) with a bootstrap CI on alpha. Report whether better large-n optima FLATTEN the decay (weakening the

evaluations.title: Doubling split-law transfer: a placement-coordinate scale-flow generator (positive complement to the failed L2 model)
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: E406 showed a global one-mode L2 scale-aware coupling model does not transfer; E409 showed why (area is a width-scale placement functional, so L2-closeness is the wrong metric). This experiment tests the positive complement in placement coordinates: a doubling within-pair split-law. Each optimized child (2n) construction is decomposed as an affine image of its parent (n) plus a within-pair SPLIT; the split is expressed in CHILD- WIDTH units w~1/(2n) and fit as a transferable law F across the cascade {8->16,16->32,32->64,64->128} with one step HELD OUT. We then GENERATE the held-out child with zero exact optimization and measure exact area, with pre-registered

evaluations.title: Feasibility probe: exact rational offset-cell global optimization at n=4
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
Test whether the exact rational offset-cell enumeration that settled the reduced n=3 model
(Eval #377) can be pushed to n=4 (3 free offsets) to close the open global-optimum bracket
[0.24943729240689047, 0.25] (Eval #58, adopted by Archive #34). Primary deliverable is a
feasibility verdict: the exact certified min-area (if enumeration closes), or the cell-count /
runtime wall and the tightest exact bracket achieved. Theorist exact-arithmetic probe, not a
score submission.

evaluations.title: Feasibility-aware role-calendar screen
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Archive #10/#11/#12/#32-style feasibility and compatibility screens can distinguish useful component-boundary calendars from wrong scaffolds before polishing. Apply simplified slab-pattern and side/order consistency diagnostics to role-calendar candidates from Eval #401 and compare the diagnostics with raw exact area and polish outcomes.

evaluations.title: Theory Probe: Fracture Mechanics Pipeline and Threshold Tuning (n=64)
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: We implement the first Dynamic Fracture Pipeline for generative scaffolds. We treat the 16x4 scaffold not as a static geometric box, but as a network of quadratic springs pulling edge heights to y=0.5. If the exact area gradient stretches a spring past a critical threshold tau, the spring irreversibly fractures. We tune tau to observe how the network yields and which false constraints survive as the load-bearing skeleton.

evaluations.title: Role-movie audit tooling foundation
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable component-boundary role audit layer for realized Kakeya union movies, using exact area only for validation and sampled role movies for interpretable feature extraction. This is the first approved Tick 440-500 component-boundary role calculus work package; success is a clean artifact and baseline diagnostics, not a new score.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact Hessian Active-Edge Density of Raw Scaffolds (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: A non-generative diagnostic extracting the exact active contact graph from previously generated raw scaffolds. Tests the hypothesis that strict surrogates (Eval 395) polish well because they manufacture a dense network of exact topological creases (high non-zero off-diagonal Hessian elements), whereas soft surrogates (Eval 405) polish poorly because their raw scaffolds lack active geometric collisions, causing the exact polisher to stall in shallow basins.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Expanded Active-Edge Topology Metric Across Architectures (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Expands the active-edge Hessian diagnostic (Eval 416) across multiple n=64 generative architectures (Flat, Tree-Path, Spectral, CNN-MLP). Tests the hypothesis that downstream polishability is strictly predicted by the raw scaffold's topological density, identifying a 'Goldilocks' zone of active edges (~100-150) that balances gradient flow against over-constraint.

evaluations.title: Role-response dataset and stability audit
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Consolidate prior Parallax before/after candidate pairs into a reusable role-response dataset using the new role_movie.py module, and audit grid/threshold stability of the sampled role definitions. This supports later held-out prediction experiments without yet claiming predictive value.

evaluations.title: The area-relevant near-touch braid: does the discrete near-touch skeleton transfer across n, and do per-level savings explain G(n) decay?
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Phase-4 of the approved lane. Archive #35 established that the optimized advantage is a width-scale placement phenomenon: doubling transfers a good warm-start basin but no tested low-complexity rule generates competitive offsets, because the metric placement is sharp at scale w~1/n. This experiment asks whether the DISCRETE near-touch skeleton transfers even though the metric placement does not. Since the exact area is piecewise- linear in offsets, the optimum is a vertex of an arrangement whose active constraints are near-touch events (sorted-adjacent endpoint coincidences). I extract, from the best-known offsets at each n, the area-relevant adjacent-transposition braid: the set of sorted-position-adjacent endpoint

evaluations.title: Exact 2D-slice arrangement enumeration at n=4: validating cell-quadratic machinery and deriving the plateau wall coefficients from cell geometry
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
Gate-scoped theorist prototype. Eval #412 showed axis-aligned box B&B cannot
certify the n=4 optimum because it cannot prune the flat plateau tube. This
evaluation tests whether exact breakpoint-order CELL enumeration, restricted to
the 2D slice x1=1/4 (x4=0 gauge, variables x2,x3), can (a) reproduce the Eval #97
plateau/wall formulas purely from assembled cell quadratics without hard-coding
them, and (b) yield a reusable cell-atlas artifact. This is a non-score diagnostic
/ tool-building stage; success is defined by exact-arithmetic faithfulness and the
gate-(a) reconstruction, not by score.

evaluations.title: Theory Probe: Dynamic Fracture Penalty Sweep (lambda vs tau=0.05)
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps the constraint spring stiffness lambda in [0.1, 1.0, 10.0] against a tight displacement threshold tau=0.05. Measures post-fracture geometric displacement to distinguish between catalytic width-scale relaxation and parasitic macroscopic sprawling.

evaluations.title: Grouped held-out role-response ablation
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether stable sampled role-response features from Eval 418 add held-out triage or regression value beyond sampled geometry/width baselines. This is a non-score diagnostic ablation with group-aware splits and strict no-overclaim reporting.

evaluations.title: Robustness of the U-shaped per-level savings signature: across seeds and across reference baselines
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #419 found that, relative to Keich, the optimized-minus-Keich per-dyadic-level savings advantage is U-shaped: positive at the coarsest and finest levels and negative in the middle, across n=8..128. Before presenting this as an actionable scale-design heuristic, this experiment runs falsification-first due-diligence to determine whether the U-shape is (i) a robust property of independent good constructions or (ii) an artifact of the Keich reference or of a single optimizer seed. Two controls: (A) recompute the per-level savings signature across MULTIPLE independent near-optimal seeds at each n and report variability; (B) recompute the per-level signature relative to DIFFERENT reference baselines (Keich, the

evaluations.title: Role-event casebook and counter-specimens
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Reframe fragile sampled role-response quantities as localized event labels rather than aggregate predictors. Build a deterministic role-event extractor and a counter-specimen casebook from the Eval 418/422 candidate-pair dataset, focusing on admissible narratives, false friends, and equal-area differentiators rather than score improvement.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Topological Buckling via False Tension Injection (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests the core transport mechanism of the Generative Exact-Acceptance lane: can injecting explicit 'false tension' into a stable active tree transport the geometry into a better exact basin? This diagnostic takes the exact Keich active tree, injects a single high-weight sacrificial constraint (P_ij) that violates the current topology, and projects the resulting tension network. We test if the resulting warped geometry (the 'buckle') polishes to an exact area better than Keich.

evaluations.title: Fresh role-intentional candidate holdout
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Generate a fresh explicit-offset candidate set using pre-registered role-event stage directions and matched geometry/subgradient controls, then exact-evaluate all candidates without iterative leaderboard optimization. The goal is to test whether role-intentional moves create a different and useful candidate distribution after Eval #422/#424 showed old-log scalar roles did not add predictive signal beyond sampled geometry.

evaluations.title: Generative Transport via Active-Tree Constrained Stress Perturbation (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 'Topological Buckling' generative mechanism. Instead of generating a topology from scratch, we extract the exact active intersection tree of the incumbent, fix those weights (P_base) heavily, and optimize continuous 'false tension' parameters (Delta P, Delta Y) to minimize a smooth surrogate. Every 50 steps, the resulting warped geometry is exact-polished; if it improves, it becomes the new incumbent.

evaluations.title: 3D arrangement-atlas engine for n=4 Kakeya: facet-flip BFS characterization of the optimal-set degeneracy geometry
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Milestone of the approved arrangement-atlas lane (proposal T453-515). Eval #420 validated exact cell-quadratic machinery on the 2D slice x1=1/4 and found a flat constant-area cell (area=1/4) bordered by curvature walls (50/3, 8). This lifts the method to full gauge-fixed 3D (x4=0, vars x1,x2,x3) to characterize the OPTIMAL SET of the n=4 Kakeya area: its exact value, dimension, and bounding degeneracy geometry. The primitive is facet-flip BFS over the 3D arrangement of breakpoint-difference planes, seeded at the known plateau, with a hard exact-equality validation gate per cell. This is a theory/tool milestone; success is defined by exact faithfulness and an interpretable

evaluations.title: Role-event specificity and admissibility audit
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Audit why Eval 426's role-intentional moves and controls both triggered broad event labels. Tighten event admissibility rules and measure whether localized role-event targets distinguish intentional moves from matched controls, before any further generation is attempted.

evaluations.title: Generative Transport via Gap-Surrogate Stress Perturbation (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the depth-mispricing soft-coverage surrogate from Eval 427 with a differentiable Exact-Savings Gap Surrogate (inspired by Archive #34). Tests whether training false tensions (Delta P, Delta Y) against a geometry-faithful objective allows the continuous transport mechanism to propose macroscopic folds that pass the exact-acceptance filter and cross the 0.90x Keich target at n=32.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Topological Shattering of the 16x4 Scaffold (Eval #421 Artifact)
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: A purely algorithmic diagnostic that computes the connected components of the 42 surviving spring edges from Eval #421 to mathematically certify the 'Topological Shattering' (Tectonic Plates) hypothesis.

evaluations.title: Strict event collateral ledger
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze Eval 426/429 strict role-event false friends by decomposing local intended-event evidence from collateral width and component-count damage elsewhere. The goal is to turn failed role stage directions into admissibility rules and a failure taxonomy, not to generate new candidates.

evaluations.title: Generative Exact-Acceptance Transport via CNN Tension Proposals (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
