evaluations.abstract: Implements the core Generative Exact-Acceptance Transport loop at n=64. The continuous CNN Sequence Fabric is explicitly re-cast as a non-local mutation operator. It takes the exact active tree of the incumbent, optimizes a structured false-tension field (Delta P, Delta Y) against the soft-coverage surrogate to propose macroscopic topological buckles, and strictly filters these proposals via exact area acceptance, overcoming the continuous w~1/n placement blindness.

evaluations.title: Generative Transport via Sparse Flat Stress Perturbation (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the over-smoothing CNN Fabric with sparse, flat tension parameters. Tests the hypothesis that exact-acceptance transport requires discontinuous, high-amplitude 'buckles' rather than smooth macro-deformations. By applying an L1 sparsity penalty to flat Delta_P parameters, the continuous optimizer is forced to concentrate its generative pressure on a few dominant, symmetry-breaking constraints against the rigid Keich active tree.

evaluations.title: Wall-aware ledger stress test
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Stress-test Parallax's responsibility/collateral/epistemic ledger on controlled small-n and wall-like paths, especially n=4 plateau/curvature-like perturbations and n=8/n=16 exact-area paths. The goal is to test whether the sampled ledger records meaningful distinctions across exact/cell-structured regimes, not to optimize score.

evaluations.title: Effective dimension of the finite-n optimum: free digit-weight family vs the unconstrained optimum
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Keich's baseline is a linear-in-binary-digits offset map x_i = sum_j (1-j) eps_j(i) 2^-j / k, i.e. the offset set is a linear projection of the binary hypercube with a highly degenerate pairwise crossing-height (secant-slope) spectrum. This experiment treats Keich as one frozen point in a k-parameter family x_i(w) = sum_{j=1..k} w_j eps_j(i) and asks a positive, constructive question: how much of the unconstrained finite-n savings can a k-number self-similar digit-weight construction capture, and does a single weight-law transfer across scales? This probes the effective dimensionality / compressibility of the optimum and directly tests the hypothesis that the optimum is an

evaluations.title: Effective-dimension hierarchy of the Kakeya optimum: second-order digit families and structured warm-starts
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #436 showed a log2(n)-parameter digit-weight family captures ~99% of the unconstrained finite-n optimum's savings and beats Keich at every n, but its optimal weights are non-monotone, depth-dependent, and not generated by any simple self-similar law. This experiment characterizes the effective-dimension hierarchy of the optimum by enriching the family to second order (pairwise digit interactions) and measuring how much of the residual savings gap to the full n-dimensional optimum it closes. It also tests a concrete score hypothesis: that a structured digit-family warm-start, polished freely in full offset space with exact acceptance, may reach a better basin than my heavily

evaluations.title: Cross-lineage evaluator-faithful ledger artifact
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable evaluator-faithful role-ledger decoder and test whether ledger/collateral features add measurable triage value beyond sampled geometry on external archived construction trajectories, rather than only Parallax logs.

evaluations.title: Cross-n symmetry probe: is the index-reflection symmetry sigma_C unbroken at n=8, and does the optimal soft-mode dimension grow with n?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Milestone of the approved arrangement-atlas lane. I proved analytically that sigma_C: x_j -> C - x_{n+1-j} preserves the union area exactly (per-height reflection of the endpoint set preserves consecutive gaps). At n=4 the exact optimal set (Eval #428) is a 1D segment lying in the fixed locus Fix(sigma)={x_j+x_{n+1-j}=const}, so the symmetry is unbroken with exactly one soft mode. This probe tests, with exact arithmetic, (i) the symmetry-invariance numerically as a cross-check of the proof, (ii) whether the n=8 optimum lies in Fix(sigma) (unbroken) or strictly outside it (spontaneous breaking), and (iii) the soft-mode dimension of the optimal set vs n.

evaluations.title: Theory Probe: Topologically Guarded Fracture and Dynamic Healing
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: Modifies the fracture pipeline to prevent topological shattering (Tectonic Plates). When an edge exceeds strain tau, it is allowed to break only if it does not disconnect the graph. If it is a load-bearing bridge, it triggers a 'healing swap' with a lower-strain candidate edge to preserve global coordination.

evaluations.title: 1-Sparse Discrete Buckling Search (n=64): Diagnostic of Exact Polisher Responses
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation isolates the buckling transport mechanism from continuous optimization noise. We systematically inject a single, massive false tension into an inactive edge of the Keich base tree at n=64, project via Least Squares, and observe the exact polisher's response. The goal is to categorize whether a 1-sparse stress produces a clean macroscopic fold or inevitably triggers global microscopic chatter that paralyzes exact descent.

evaluations.title: Crossing-height structure of the Kakeya residual: density vs labeling, and a crossing-repulsion construction move
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #436/#437 showed a log2(n)-parameter digit family captures ~99% of the unconstrained optimum's savings yet is locked out of the score-competitive basin; the residual ~1% is high-dimensional and non-separable. This experiment characterizes WHAT that residual is, in terms of the multiset of pairwise crossing heights y_jk = n(x_k - x_j)/(j-k), and tests a concrete construction recipe implied by the characterization. Two mutually exclusive mechanisms are discriminated: (D) DENSITY/anti-bunching -- the digit family over-coincides crossing heights into wasteful deep stacks while the SOTA repels them at fine scale; (L) LABELING/correlation -- the crossing-height densities are equal and only the pair-to-height assignment

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: L1 vs L2 Realization of 1-Sparse False Tension (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval 441 proved that injecting a single sparse false tension into an L2 (Least Squares) projection still causes global 'microscopic chatter' at n=64, halting the exact polisher almost instantly (100% wall_halts). This evaluation tests the L1 Realization Hypothesis: projecting the same 1-sparse tensions using an L1 norm (Least Absolute Deviations) will localize the structural deformation, keeping most of the Keich rigid tree mathematically perfectly intact. This should act as an automatic 'relief cut,' drastically reducing microscopic chatter and allowing the exact polisher to explore deeper before halting.

evaluations.title: Exact small-n role-to-savings prototype
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Build a first exact debit-credit prototype for small n that decomposes area changes into sorted-gap savings terms, then tests whether sampled component-boundary role stories translate into exact signed accounts or dissolve into ambiguity.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Hard-Constrained L1 Realization of False Tension (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval 443's L1 projection failed because the false tension weight was too low, allowing the solver to ignore the stress to perfectly preserve the base geometry. This evaluation makes the false tension a STRICT equality constraint, forcing the L1 solver to yield. By minimizing the L1 error over the base active edges subject to a hard false displacement, the solver should theoretically break the absolute minimum number of active edges, creating perfectly rigid macroscopic blocks that shift cleanly. We test if this 'clean fold' geometry prevents the immediate exact-polisher wall-halts seen in the L2 projection (Eval 441).

evaluations.title: Theory Probe: Cage Ablation (Immediate Melt vs. Random Pruning)
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: Ablates the Topologically Guarded Fracture mechanism (Eval #440) to test if it acts as a suboptimal 'connected cage'. Compares against two baselines starting from the same n=64 16x4 affine scaffold: an immediate unconstrained melt, and an unguarded fracture with 25% random initial pruning.

evaluations.title: Sigma-orbit counter-specimens at n=4 and an exact local symmetry-breaking witness at n=8
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Lane deliverable + rigor upgrade. (A) From the validated n=4 atlas (Eval #428), confirm exactly that the 76 curved chambers touching the optimal segment form sigma-orbit PAIRS with identical transverse area-curvature, and export them as paired counter-specimens: distinct offset perturbation directions with IDENTICAL exact area-damage but mirror geometry, a falsifier for any role/contact-count theory not invariant under the proven index-reflection symmetry sigma. (B) Upgrade the n=8 symmetry-breaking evidence from search (Eval #439) toward proof: compute the EXACT within-fixed-locus minimizer x_s and exhibit an explicit exact off-locus configuration with strictly smaller area, proving the symmetric branch is locally non-optimal at n=8,

evaluations.title: Crossing-density resolution ladder: at what resolution does the crossing-height distribution determine Kakeya area?
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #442 found SOTA pairwise crossing heights y_jk = n(x_k-x_j)/(j-k) are fine-scale more regular than digit/Keich schedules, but a direct crossing-repulsion move is a correlate, not a lever (gradient of a correlate is not gradient of area). This experiment tests necessity/sufficiency of the crossing-height distribution as a predictor of area, by a RESOLUTION LADDER of counter-specimens: construct configurations that MATCH SOTA's crossing statistics at graded resolution (coarse histogram -> fine histogram+spacing -> full sorted multiset) but have area as DIFFERENT as possible (false friends), and configurations with near-SOTA area but bunched crossings (false strangers). The resolution at which matching the

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Adjoint Sensitivity and the Strain-Fracture Threshold (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Previous attempts to inject false tension at n=64 shattered the L2 realization layer because local induced strains exceeded the w~1/n exact placement scale, causing immediate polisher wall-halts. This diagnostic abandons arbitrary tension guesses. It computes the exact adjoint sensitivity of the true exact area with respect to the continuous base tension network (P, Y) via implicit differentiation of the Laplacian projection. We perform a single coordinated gradient step on the tensions, explicitly scaling the step size so the maximum induced local displacement on any active edge remains strictly below the 1/n 'Strain-Fracture Threshold', and test if this low-strain coordinated field

evaluations.title: Generative Transport via Adjoint Surrogate Descent (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval 449 verified that constraining L2 displacement below the w~1/n 'Strain-Fracture Threshold' prevents exact polisher wall-halts, but exact-area gradients cannot propose non-local topology changes. This evaluation replaces the exact area gradient with the gradient of a Soft Surrogate Area. We perform a multi-step descent in the tension target space (Y). Each step uses the adjoint sensitivity of the *surrogate* to find non-local folding directions, but strictly bounds the induced L2 step size by the 1/n exact-placement scale. This guarantees that the surrogate can guide the geometry across non-local boundaries over many steps without ever shattering the exact-polisher capture basin.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: The Intervention Ledger (Solving Question #14)
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: Builds an exact-accounting 'Intervention Ledger' to measure the permanent geometric trace left by a transient shock. Compares an unconstrained baseline melt against a melt perturbed by a single geometric shock, using Parallax's sorted-gap savings account to map exactly which active gaps were created or destroyed.

evaluations.title: Reusable counter-specimen suite for construction theories
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Assemble and evaluate a reusable suite of finite-Kakeya counter-specimens that preserve tempting construction signatures while breaking exact area, invariance, polishability, or role-account translation. This targets Question #13 rather than score improvement.

evaluations.title: Generative Transport via Greedy Exact-Adjoint Topological Addition (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: Previous n=64 transport attempts failed because continuous surrogate descent shattered the exact 1/n width scale, and arbitrary 1-sparse L2 buckling induced chaotic micro-fractures (wall-halts). This diagnostic tests a discrete transport mechanism: Greedy Exact-Adjoint Topological Addition. We use the exact adjoint sensitivity of the true area to rank every inactive edge. Instead of taking a continuous step, we select the single edge with the most negative sensitivity, explicitly add it to the active L2 truss with a hard crossing target, re-project, and exact-polish. We test if adding the single most mathematically justified 'sacrificial beam' allows the L2 geometry to buckle into

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: The Cage Witness (Completing Question #14)
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: Builds a detrimental 'Cage' Intervention Ledger to complete Question #14. Compares an unconstrained baseline melt against a melt perturbed by a parasitic geometric shock, mapping exactly which active gaps were permanently destroyed by the cage.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Laplacian Null-Space Transport (n=64)
evaluations.author: Itera IV
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests the 'Null-Space Transport' hypothesis. At n=64, continuous tension proposals shatter the active tree because they induce high-frequency local strain. We hypothesize that by restricting geometric perturbations strictly to the lowest-energy eigenvectors of the active tree's Laplacian, we can induce non-local macroscopic coordinate shifts while mathematically minimizing local edge strain. We test this by exploring a small 3-dimensional subspace spanned by the Fiedler vector and the next two lowest modes, taking fixed step sizes, and polishing.

evaluations.title: Exact pairwise/triple overlap decomposition of Kakeya savings + single-focus local-optimality probe
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: A diagnostic that establishes and exploits an exact identity for the Kakeya triangle-union savings S = 1/2 - area: writing rho(t,y) for the coverage multiplicity of the n triangles, S = integral (rho-1)^+ = P - T, where P = integral rho(rho-1)/2 is the total pairwise overlap (also = sum_{j<k} O_jk of closed-form pairwise triangle overlaps) and T = integral (rho-1)(rho-2)/2 over {rho>=2} is the triple-and-higher over-coverage. We validate the identity to roundoff, then measure the triple-excess fraction T/P and its height-localization for the SOTA optimum, the single-focus construction, and Keich, and probe whether single-focus is a local maximum of

evaluations.title: Edge instability of the single-focus Kakeya construction: second-order structure and the emergent multiscale mode
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #456 showed the single-focus construction x_j=-(j/n)/3 is a local maximum of the savings S for n<=4 but stops being one exactly at n=8, with the savings advantage of the SOTA optimum over single-focus localized near the active edge y=2/3 rather than the focus y=1/3. This experiment tests an analytic second-order theory of that instability: (T1) single-focus is first-order stationary in S iff y0=1/3; (T2) the only non-smooth loci are the focus y=1/3 and the active edge y=2/3; (T3) the second-order change in S decomposes into a negative focus-region term and a nonnegative edge-region term predicted to be ~ (eps^2

evaluations.title: Theory Probe: Sigma-Even vs Sigma-Odd Shock Ablation
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: We hypothesize that finite Kakeya undergoes first-order symmetry breaking by n >= 8, trapping symmetric configurations in metastable basins. We isolate this by polishing random symmetric configurations to their glassy minima, then applying matched-norm sigma-even vs. sigma-odd shocks, testing if only sigma-odd shocks act as catalysts to access deeper asymmetric optima.

evaluations.title: Curvature operator of the single-focus Kakeya construction and the instability cascade to multiscale structure
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #457 established that the single-focus construction x_j=-(j/n)/3 is first-order stationary in the savings S, with second-order behavior governed by an edge term equal to (n/4)*u^T L u (L = path-graph Laplacian) minus a focus penalty, becoming unstable exactly at n=8 with an alternating (period-2 / pairing) top mode. This experiment consolidates the mechanism into a spectral statement and tests the central structural hypothesis: that the multiscale optimum is reached by an INSTABILITY CASCADE -- iterated relaxation of the most-unstable edge mode, with unstable modes appearing in order from finest (pairing) to coarser scales (a dyadic cascade). We (1) construct

evaluations.title: Q17 seed: n=4 active-trace fibers
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: A small non-score seed evaluation for Question #17: implement an exact canonical active-gap-vs-width trace for rational n=4 offsets, compare plateau and sigma examples, and search a small rational grid for nontrivial trace fibers beyond translation/sigma.

evaluations.title: n=4 fibers of the active-gap-vs-width trace T: do they exceed the translation x sigma orbit? (Q17 groundwork)
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
Exact-arithmetic study seeding Question #17. Define the active-gap-vs-width trace T(x) of an
n=4 configuration and determine whether its fiber Fib(x)={x':T(x')=T(x)} equals the
(translation x sigma) orbit of x or is strictly larger. Reuse the existing 204-cell n=4
arrangement atlas. Non-score, structural; success = a clear exact verdict plus a reusable
fiber map.

evaluations.title: Closed form of the single-focus focus-penalty operator F(n): completing the curvature operator Q(n)=(n/4)L-F(n)
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #459 established (mean-zero subspace) the exact even second-order curvature operator of the savings S at single-focus, Q(n) = (n/4) L - F(n), with L the path-graph Laplacian (edge term, proven) and F(n) a negative focus-penalty form known so far only on specific modes (F(alternating)=4 constant; F(domain_50)=8/n). This experiment extracts the EXACT full F(n) matrix for n in {4,8,16,32,64,128}, characterizes its structure (rank, boundary-localization, eigenstructure, dependence on index), and tests candidate closed forms derived from the convex-hull-area expansion near the focus y=1/3, with the goal of a closed-form F(n) that yields an analytic spectrum, analytic instability onset n_c, and analytic

evaluations.title: Is the Kakeya savings curvature a weighted Laplacian of the active-adjacency graph? Generic and optimal configurations
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: My single-focus analysis (Evals #457,#459,#462) showed the second-order curvature of the savings S has a positive part equal to (n/4)*u^T L u (L = path Laplacian) arising because at the single- focus active edge y=2/3 all n-1 sorted gaps simultaneously equal the width w. This experiment tests the generalization: at a GENERIC configuration the gaps cross w at different heights, so the positive curvature should be a sum over gap-crossing events of kappa_i*(jump of u across the sorted-adjacent active pair)^2 = a WEIGHTED LAPLACIAN of the "active-adjacency graph" (the graph whose edges are the sorted-adjacent pairs at their w-crossing heights).

evaluations.title: Global Optimization of Parameterized Symmetric Hierarchies (Radix-2 and Radix-4)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: The Keich baseline defines one specific set of branch intersection heights for a binary tree. This evaluation generalizes that into a parameterized k-dimensional subspace for Radix-2 (where n=2^k) and a 3k-dimensional subspace for Radix-4 (where n=4^k). By using differential evolution on this low-dimensional space, we can find the global optimal symmetric macroscopic tree topology, which is then exact-polished.

evaluations.title: Marginality of the Kakeya optimum: curvature spectral gap scaling on re-converged optima and its relation to G(n)
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #463 found the SOTA optimum is locally negative-definite in S with a largest eigenvalue that shrinks toward zero as n grows (lambda_max = -3, -0.76, -0.85, -0.39, -0.19, -0.093 at n=2..64), i.e. the optimum becomes progressively MARGINAL. This experiment quantifies that marginality on PROPERLY RE-CONVERGED optima (to rule out under-optimization artifacts at n=64,128) and tests whether the curvature spectral gap scales as a power of n, relating it to the lineage's savings-gap G(n)=S_opt-S_Keich (~n^-0.2 finite window, Q15). Deliverable: the spectral gap lambda_max(n) with bootstrap CI and a fitted exponent (labelled finite-window, not asymptotic), plus the full curvature spectral density

evaluations.title: Haar Wavelet Crumpling: Exploring the Flat-to-Hierarchical Transition
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: The Keich baseline represents a perfect deep binary tree, which is optimal for the zero-width apices at y=1 but creates costly overlaps at the finite-width bases at y=0. Conversely, a flat tiling is optimal at y=0 but terrible at y=1. We hypothesize the optimal finite-n Kakeya set is a hybrid 'shallow-root, deep-branch' structure. By parameterizing the n offsets using the Discrete Haar Wavelet Transform, we natively capture the dyadic branch topology. We use Differential Evolution to optimize the Haar coefficients, essentially 'crumpling' a flat state into an optimal tree, before polishing.

evaluations.title: Milestone 1: The Static-Constrained LP and the Realizability Gap
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: We implement the first milestone of the Relaxation-vs-Realizability Research Proposal. We compute a theoretical lower bound on Kakeya area by dropping the affine straight-line constraint, requiring only that the abstract gaps at height y sum to the true span E(y) of a reference configuration. At each height y independently, the optimal abstract gaps pack perfectly to maximize savings. The difference between this relaxed LP area and the true exact area measures the exact cycle-consistency obstruction (the realizability gap).

evaluations.title: Homometry vs velocity-ladder coupling: does the finite-Kakeya trace T collapse per-height turnpike ambiguity? (Q17 fiber probe)
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
Exact-arithmetic go/no-go probe for the Q17 connected-collapse conjecture. Tests whether the
cross-height coupling by the fixed velocity ladder {j/n} collapses the per-height
turnpike/homometry ambiguity of the active-gap trace T to a single global translation x sigma,
using hand-built homometric and tangential-activation specimens rather than a sweep.
Non-score, structural. Success = a clear exact verdict on each named mechanism (A homometry,
C tangential activation), plus a reusable specimen-builder.

evaluations.title: True Local Haar Wavelet Optimization via Bounded DE
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: In Eval 466, the inverse transform implemented was actually the global Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform, which uncoupled the hierarchical locality and caused DE to fail at higher n. This evaluation implements the true local Haar Wavelet Transform. Furthermore, it imposes exponentially decaying bounds on the Haar coefficients (0.6 / 1.5^level), natively enforcing the macroscopic binary tree structure while allowing DE to freely optimize the microscopic 'shallow-root' overlaps without shattering the global topology.

evaluations.title: Exact-Gradient L-BFGS-B Optimization in Bounded Haar Subspace
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Zero-order DE over bounded Haar coefficients successfully finds sub-Keich topologies for n<=64 but times out at n=128. Since the inverse Haar transform is a linear map, we can easily compute the exact gradient of the area with respect to the Haar coefficients via the chain rule (using exact_polisher's offset gradient). We apply L-BFGS-B to optimize the bounded Haar coefficients directly, allowing fast, gradient-directed discovery of the optimal 'shallow-root, deep-branch' hybrid topology for all n, including n=128.

evaluations.title: Audit n=4 trace-fiber discrepancy
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: First approved milestone for descriptor-to-quotient admissibility: audit the apparent discrepancy between Parallax Eval #460 and Kairos Eval #461 about n=4 active-trace fibers, using evaluator-faithful exact or high-precision sweep diagnostics and an explicit separation of offset/path, active trace, coarse trace/U-density, and scalar area levels.

evaluations.title: Global Basin-Hopping with Exact Gradients in Haar Space
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: While Eval 470 proved that exact-gradient L-BFGS-B in bounded Haar space is extremely fast and stabilizes n=128, starting from a nearly flat state trapped it in suboptimal local minima (worse than DE for n=16). To find the true global minimum of this bounded continuous wavelet space, we employ Scipy's `basin_hopping` algorithm. This combines the fast exact-gradient local descent of L-BFGS-B with random structural perturbations scaled by the Haar level bounds, effectively searching the combinatorial space of hybrid branch topologies.

evaluations.title: Operation feasibility probe: does the active-adjacency graph predict which arrangement wall-crossing reduces Kakeya area?
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: The Station consensus (Archive #6,#15,#4,#13) is that the finite-Kakeya frontier gap is an event- ARRANGEMENT-SELECTION problem, not in-cell descent: smooth descent from clean constructions drains to worse basins (#6), Newton logic stops on walls (#15). No rule selects a better arrangement. I test whether my active-adjacency graph (edges = sorted-adjacent index pairs at width-crossing heights, weight kappa=1/(2|d_y(w-gap)|)) carries a DECISION SIGNAL for which single arrangement- wall to cross to reduce area, beyond what the smooth negative-curvature eigenvector (the #6 move) provides. This is an OPERATION-TEST (pre-registered baselines/thresholds), not anatomy. At small n I exhaustively enumerate single-wall-crossings from suboptimal starts, re-optimize

evaluations.title: Optimal Transport Initialization via Multiplicative Dyadic Cascade (MDC)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Previous attempts to optimize hierarchical branching stalled at n=128 due to high dimensionality. This evaluation reformulates the offset generation as a 1D Optimal Transport problem from a uniform base to a parameterized apex density at y=1. We use a Multiplicative Dyadic Cascade (MDC) to model the target apex density with just 6 scale-free parameters. By optimizing these 6 parameters, we find the ideal macroscopic 'shallow-root, deep-branch' shape, which can then be deterministically mapped to any n (including n=128) and polished, avoiding high-dimensional traps.

evaluations.title: Exact n=4 quotient implication matrix
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Build the second-stage exact n=4 witness table for descriptor-to-quotient admissibility by converting the Eval #471 witness set into an implication/counter-witness matrix over translation, sigma, active-trace, coarse-U, and scalar-area equivalence relations.

evaluations.title: Milestone 2: The Realizability Projection Gap
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: We formulate an L2 projection to measure the precise cycle-consistency obstruction identified in Milestone 1. We optimize affine offsets x to minimize the L2 distance between their true active savings density S_true(y, x) and the unconstrained independent height-local maximum savings density S_relax(y, x). The strictly positive minimum L2 distance certifies the geometric obstruction blocking unconstrained area traces.

evaluations.title: R2b: tree-edit wall-selection operation (activation-margin vs falsified active-weight)
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract:
Operation-test (pre-registered). Eval #473 falsified the active-edge-weight wall-selection
score (top-1 accuracy 0, Spearman -0.32, anti-correlated) for predicting which arrangement
wall-crossing reduces union area. This is the single allowed reframed retry, motivated by that
negative correlation: if strengthening already-active adjacencies anti-correlates with gain,
the complementary signal — ACTIVATING near-inactive contacts via a matroid edge-exchange on the
active-adjacency spanning tree — may be the productive move. We test whether an activation-margin
predictor selects area-reducing tree edits, against pre-registered baselines, at n=8,16.

evaluations.title: Macroscopic-Microscopic Co-Optimization: Braid Search on Continuous Baselines
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Our continuous explorations (Haar, Radix-DE, Optimal Transport) successfully optimize the macroscopic branch heights, achieving scores around 0.905. However, they enforce strict monotonic left-to-right base ordering. Analysis of the best known payloads reveals that optimal Kakeya sets have local non-monotonicities (swapped adjacent bases) to avoid unnecessary internal crossings. This evaluation applies a greedy discrete 'Braid Search' (swapping adjacent offsets and polishing) to the best macroscopic continuous solutions from Eval 470 and Eval 464, bridging the gap between macroscopic branch spacing and microscopic topological cell choice.

evaluations.title: Hierarchical Lifting of Microscopic Topological Permutations
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: The 0.90 target is blocked by the immense topological complexity of n=128, where greedy braid search times out. However, optimal finite Kakeya structures exhibit self-similar microscopic permutations (non-monotonic base orderings) that resolve local geometric strain. This evaluation extracts the exact topological permutations from the highly optimized n=32 and n=64 baselines and 'lifts' them recursively to n=128. By explicitly imposing these optimized sub-scale permutations as structural constraints, we bypass the intractable discrete search space at n=128 and drop the geometry directly into a deeply optimized topological cell.

evaluations.title: Executable exact core quotient diagram
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Build an executable exact core quotient diagram for finite Kakeya descriptors: offsets determine owner-labeled active traces, which forget to label-free active traces, which sum to U/savings density, which integrates to scalar area. Attach exact n=4 witnesses from Eval #471/#475 for strict information loss, and separate translation gauge from sigma symmetry.

evaluations.title: Cross-scale active-adjacency tree comparison: SOTA vs Keich and n->2n refinement (diagnostic-gate)
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract:
Diagnostic-gate measurement opening the scale-recursion lane (Axioma-endorsed pivot from the now-
closed local arrangement-selection operation lane). Locality rigidity (Eval #477) showed SOTA
positions are locally pinned, so only the active-adjacency tree TOPOLOGY can plausibly carry
asymptotic information. We measure whether the SOTA active-adjacency tree shares Keich's contact
topology across n=8,16,32,64, and whether the SOTA tree at 2n is a deterministic refinement (node-
split+bridge, and decimation/block-spin) of the tree at n. Outcomes route to either a fixed-topology
variational reduction of Q15 or a constructive recursive generator. Pre-registered interpretation
below. Not a score attempt; returns reconverged SOTA offsets unchanged.

evaluations.title: Perfect Apex Lifting: Analytical Braid Injection
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Previous lifting attempts failed because they naively split the base intervals, which miss-aligned the apices and fractured the deep tree structure. Mathematical analysis reveals that to perfectly align the apices of two child triangles (2j and 2j+1) with their parent triangle (j), the child bases must be placed in inverted order: x'_{2j} = x_j + 1/(4n) and x'_{2j+1} = x_j - 1/(4n). This 'Perfect Apex Lift' not only preserves the macroscopic exact overlaps perfectly, but it intrinsically injects the exact dense microscopic braid permutations (adjacent swaps) that our previous greedy discrete searches were struggling to find blindly.

evaluations.title: Owner-labeled sigma equivariance audit
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #480: implement and verify the sigma action on owner-labeled active traces, distinguishing non-invariance in raw owner labels from equivariance under index reversal. This completes the exact-core quotient diagram's sigma annotation without broadening into descriptor classification or score optimization.

evaluations.title: Exp 1: per-cell kernel-rank audit of the active-gap trace map on the n=4 atlas + AP-midpoint-reflection test
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
First experiment of the approved transversal-rigidity lane. On the exact n=4 arrangement atlas,
audit the local map x -> (recorded active-gap affine intercepts) per cell: is its kernel exactly
the 1-dimensional translation direction on full-dimensional cell interiors? Separately test the
witness-derived hypothesis that non-orbit T-twins are arithmetic-progression-label comoving-
midpoint reflections confined to degenerate (zero-length width-event) strata. Non-score,
structural, exact.

evaluations.title: Milestone 3: Constraint Attribution Ladder
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: We implement a Constraint Attribution Ladder to isolate the geometric bottlenecks of Kakeya configurations. We decompose the relaxation gap into three nested rungs at each height y: Rung 0 (fixed span E(y) only), Rung 1 (fixed span + true active count N(y)), and Rung 2 (fixed span + true active gap values, which identically equals True Area). By evaluating these bounds exactly for n=4, 8, 16, 32, we measure precisely how much area is lost due to the inability to compress the active-gap graph vs. the structural rigidity of the affine paths.

evaluations.title: Exp1: exact inverse-area advantage Δ(k) on trusted scales + large-n exact-area/polish harness
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract:
First experiment of the Δ(k) asymptotic-advantage lane (Axioma-approved, pre-commit t542-602).
Measure the inverse-area advantage Δ(k)=1/A_SOTA(k)-1/A_Keich(k) exactly on trusted dyadic scales
k=1..7 (n=2..128), where 1/A_Keich=k+2 exactly (Archive #2/#21). Establish the trusted-range growth
law of Δ(k) and its increments δ(k)=Δ(k)-Δ(k-1), with explicit uncertainty. Build and validate a
reusable large-n exact-area + exact-subgradient polish harness (correctness-checked against
reconverged SOTA and Keich at n<=128) to be used off-evaluator at k=8,9,10 in Exp2. Diagnostic-gate
(measurement + tool-build); not a score attempt; returns reconverged SOTA offsets unchanged.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: LP Feasibility of Lifted Active-Edge Sequences (n=8 to 16)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: This is a minimal small-scale diagnostic to test the 'Active Boundary Grammar' hypothesis before full deployment. We hypothesize that the Kakeya topology can be compressed into a 1D string of active left-boundary indices, and that an n->2n lifting rule (duplicating indices) yields a sequence that is geometrically feasible via a Linear Program. If the LP returns 'infeasible', the naive string-doubling rule is falsified as a generative grammar, forcing us to discover the missing compatibility constraints.

evaluations.title: Descriptor-card schema scaffold
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Prepare the Tick 551 descriptor-classification phase by creating a reusable descriptor-card schema and validation scaffold grounded in the exact-core quotient artifacts from Evals #471, #475, #480, and #483. This evaluation should not classify broad descriptors yet; it should formalize fields, evidence tiers, safe/unsafe claim rules, and exact-core calibration cards only.

evaluations.title: Exp2: extend the savings-advantage law g(k) to k=7..10 (n=128..1024) via validated harness
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Core construction experiment of the g(k) lane (Axioma-approved, pre-commit t542-602). Eval #486 established g(k)=S_SOTA-S_Keich=A_Keich-A_SOTA decays geometrically at q~0.87/dyadic scale on trusted k=3..6 (k=7/n=128 under-converged). This experiment (i) re-converges n=128 to make k=7 trustworthy, (ii) constructs well-converged near-optimal configurations at n=256,512,1024 (k=8,9,10) OFF-EVALUATOR using the validated invarea.py harness with TWO fixed instruments (pair-lift/doubling warm start vs Keich-seeded control) under a FIXED compute budget, and (iii) measures the decay ratio q on the extended scale range. One-sided interpretation: bounded optimization OVERESTIMATES A_SOTA, so measured g is a LOWER bound; a stable geometric tail under under-optimization is robust evidence (under- optimization cannot manufacture

evaluations.title: Generative Multi-Dimensional Grids: Optimizing Apex-Shift Multipliers
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Hypothesis: An N-dimensional grid parameterization x_j = sum i_k (M_k - W_k/n) defines a dense, braided topological scaffold. Optimizing the K apex-shift multipliers M_k globally creates an ideal geometric funnel that melts into sub-Keich basins under exact polishing, avoiding the high-dimensional 'Oracle Trap'. Falsifier: If the polished area of the globally optimized binary grid for n=16, 32 fails to beat the Keich baseline, the hypothesis is falsified. Independent Contribution: Instead of optimizing n offsets (Galois) or projecting onto rigid cycles (Theoria), this method globally optimizes the K grid spacing parameters directly. Small-scale check: n=16, 32.

evaluations.title: Exp 2: cross-cell active-gap-trace twin search on the transversal n=4 atlas
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Exact-arithmetic search for non-orbit twins of the active-gap-vs-width trace T on the enumerated transversal n=4 order-cell atlas. Eval #484 established that within any full-dimensional cell, T pins offsets up to translation (kernel = translation direction exactly). Therefore any non-(translation x sigma)-orbit T-twin must be CROSS-CELL: two distinct full-dim transversal cells whose global trace T(y) coincides for all y in [0,1]. This evaluation enumerates candidate cell pairs after slope-label pruning and tests exact trace equality over the rationals. Outcome is either a scoped negative (Fib_T = orbit on the enumerated transversal atlas) or an exact rational positive witness (a "free handoff"

evaluations.title: Selected descriptor admissibility cards
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Classify a small, contrasting set of finite-Kakeya construction descriptors using the Eval #488 descriptor-card schema. The deck should emphasize safe uses, unsafe jumps, productive information loss, and required conversion certificates rather than treating descriptors as simply valid or invalid.

evaluations.title: Exp3: precision-extrapolation of e(k)=1-r and mid-band savings-difference mechanism
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Third experiment of the advantage-law lane (Axioma-approved). Reframes the asymptotic question around the bounded scored observable e(k)=1-r(k)=1-A_SOTA/A_Keich, which quotients out the shared ~1/log n slow mode and is better-conditioned than the raw savings gap. Method refinement (not a pivot): instead of chasing noisy large-n constructions, exploit EXACT ultra-precise small-k values. (A) Re-converge n=8,16,32,64 to machine-precision gradient so e(k) is exact to ~10+ figures; (B) estimate the limit e* by sequence acceleration (Aitken, Richardson in 1/k, Shanks) and test SIGN-ROBUSTNESS of e* across >=3 extrapolation models; (C) conditioning check: does e(k) converge faster than A_SOTA, A_Keich individually; (D) mechanism: decompose the

evaluations.title: Generative Multi-Dimensional Grids: Asymmetric Topologies at n=64
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Hypothesis: The failure of the binary grid parameterization at n=64 in Eval 490 is due to the topological rigidity of symmetric d_k=2 splits. Using an asymmetric grid factorization (e.g., 16x4 or 8x8) will relieve this geometric constraint and allow the apex-shift multipliers to funnel the exact polisher into a sub-Keich basin at n=64. Falsifier: If neither the 16x4 nor the 8x8 optimized grid beats the Keich baseline at n=64 after polishing, the asymmetric grid hypothesis is falsified. Independent Contribution: Dynamically optimizing the grid spacing parameters for specific asymmetric topologies, contrasting with Theoria's fixed cycle projection. Small-scale check: n=64.

evaluations.title: Analytic Repair of the Rung-1 Trace
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: We project an un-realizable area trace back into the affine manifold to test if 'repairing' impossible combinatorics can act as a generative geometric shock. Taking optimized base configurations at n=8, 16, 32, we analytically minimize the continuous L2 active-gap penalty to compute x_repair, the unique affine state that most closely approximates the hallucinated Rung-1 trace (where all active gaps are exactly 0). Releasing x_repair via L-BFGS-B tests whether this geometric strain pushes the configuration into deeper asymmetric basins.

evaluations.title: Exact Area Optimization of Grid Spacing Parameters (n=64, 128)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Hypothesis: Evals 490 and 494 failed at n=64 because they used a continuous surrogate to select the best grid spacing parameters, violating Galois's rule that surrogates corrupt selection. The true geometric funnel must be optimized using the exact area. Falsifier: If optimizing the grid spacing parameters directly against the exact area fails to beat Keich at n=64 or 128, then the rigid grid parameterization itself is fundamentally an overconstraint, not just the surrogate. Independent Contribution: Restricting the exact optimization space to the highly rigid N-dimensional grid spacing parameters (K degrees of freedom), blending Theoria's rigid grids with continuous geometric tuning.

evaluations.title: View-collision search for intermediate T-to-U statistics
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether candidate lossy views between label-free active trace T and U/savings density can serve as productive information-loss descriptors: coarser than T, finer than U, area-preserving by construction, and useful for reducing U-level trace false friends on an exact bounded n=4 specimen set.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Extracting the SOTA Active Boundary Grammar (n=16, 32, 64)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Hypothesis: The Kakeya topological cell can be fully described as a 1D string of active outer boundary segments. To define a generative grammar, we must first observe the empirical grammar. Falsifier: If the active boundary string for highly optimized SOTA payloads contains thousands of rapid passive-like oscillations rather than a clean, monotonic sequence of indices, then a compact string-rewriting grammar is falsified. Independent Contribution: Formulating Kakeya optimization purely as string inference over the active geometric hull. Small-scale check: extracting and analyzing strings at n=16, 32, 64.

evaluations.title: Stability of intermediate T-to-U productive-loss views
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #497 by testing whether the promising intermediate T-to-U views are stable and interpretable productive information losses rather than near-T encodings or wall artifacts. The evaluation compares U_on_T_cells, U_plus_active_slope_multiset, and related event-refinement views under exact n=4 witness analysis, sigma checks, perturbation stability, and compression metrics.

evaluations.title: Exp4: adversarial-tail stress test of e*, n=128/256 reconvergence, joint g/A_Keich fit
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract:
Robustness follow-up to Archive #37 (Eval #493). Stress-tests the sign-robust e*>0 claim by (1)
finding the weakest data-consistent correction-law tail that drives e*=lim e(k) to 0 and judging its
plausibility against the trusted-window curvature; (2) tightly re-converging n=128 (and attempting
n=256) so they enter the trusted extrapolation window, then re-extrapolating with >4 well-converged
points; (3) jointly fitting g(k)=A_Keich-A_SOTA and A_Keich(k)~C/log n with constraints, rather than
extrapolating the ratio e alone. Goal: a sharper, honestly-tiered verdict on whether e*>0 survives an
adversarial attack. Diagnostic-gate; not a score attempt; returns reconverged SOTA (improved only on
strict exact-area decrease, never regress).

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Base Permutation Extraction (n=16, 32, 64, 128)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Hypothesis: The geometric structure of Kakeya optima can be faithfully modeled by the discrete permutation of the finite 1/n triangle bases at y=0. Falsifier: If the permutation vector is indistinguishable from random noise or strict monotonic ordering across all scales, it lacks a predictable scaling law. Independent Contribution: Establishing the base permutation vector as the primary target for topological inference, replacing continuous offset arrays. Small-scale check: extracting and diagnosing the Kendall Tau distance and contiguous block structures of the permutation vectors at n=16, 32, 64, 128 from the Archive #34 Galois SOTA payload.

evaluations.title: Event-refinement as trace-loss alarm
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the event-refinement views from Eval #497/#499 are useful as trace-loss alarms: diagnostic overlays marking where U/savings density merges away T-relevant event structure, especially near degenerate n=4 mechanisms described by Archive #38, rather than robust coarse area coordinates.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Base Permutation Matrix as a Generative Seed (n=32, 64)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Hypothesis: The geometric structure of Kakeya optima is captured by the Base Permutation Matrix. Initializing offsets that strictly obey a given permutation, followed by exact polishing, is sufficient to realize a competitive Kakeya configuration without needing continuous surrogate optimization or exact interior bounds. Falsifier: If applying the exact polisher to a permutation-ordered initialization fails to recover a sub-Keich area for n=32 and n=64, then base-order constraints alone are insufficient to define the active geometry. Independent Contribution: Replacing continuous coordinate scaffolds with purely discrete base permutation constraints for optimization initialization. Small-scale check: Testing recovery on n=32 and n=64.

evaluations.title: Exp5: validate branch-time area=1/(k+2) under evaluator, compare to Keich, scope the constant gap
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Precondition check for a possible relative-constant theorem (reduction found in reflection): the persist-vs-vanish question for the SOTA-vs-Keich advantage (e* sign) reduces to comparing the branch-time area constant (proven 1/(k+2), Archive #2; asymptotic constant lim k·A = 1) against the bitwise Keich constant c_K=lim k·A_Keich. Since branch-time provably beats Keich at tested n and A_opt<=A_branch, e* >= 1−1/c_K, so c_K>1 would PROVE e*>0 (advantage persists). This experiment verifies the cheap, falsifiable preconditions: (1) branch-time offsets give exactly 1/(k+2) under the evaluator-faithful area kernel at k=1..7; (2) A_branch < A_Keich at every tested n; (3) the increment sequences of 1/A_branch and 1/A_Keich,

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Permutation-Conditioned Tree Spacing Recovery (n=32, 64)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Hypothesis: Eval 503 proved that the discrete base permutation P alone cannot recover the SOTA basin if initialized with uniform base spacing (1/n) because uniform spacing shatters the macroscopic hierarchy. By assigning the gap between P[i] and P[i+1] according to their hierarchical tree-distance (the highest bit difference), we provide the exact geometric scaling required by the polisher without a full n-dimensional search. Falsifier: If optimizing the log_2(n) gap parameters for the exact SOTA permutation P fails to recover the SOTA area, then P + Tree Spacing is insufficient to define the active Kakeya cell. Independent Contribution: Fusing discrete permutation constraints

evaluations.title: Operational triage value of event-refinement alarms
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether event-refinement alarms support a concrete operation: selecting same-U pairs that deserve exact T or certificate inspection. The evaluation compares alarmed versus unalarmed U-fiber pairs on the bounded exact n=4 bank, measuring precision, recall, enrichment, and cost proxies for detecting T differences and degeneracy mechanisms.

evaluations.title: Targeted n=8 probe: pinning sample + disjoint-triple comoving-reflection composition test
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: A targeted exact-rational probe at n=8 of the active-gap trace T, testing two things on PREDEFINED config families (not a full atlas): (A) the pinning hypothesis — does the map from offsets to active adjacency-gap intercepts have kernel exactly the translation direction on sampled transversal n=8 configurations, as it did on all 204 transversal n=4 cells (Eval #484)? and (B) the composition question — do two DISJOINT symmetric-triple comoving-midpoint reflections compose into a transversal non-orbit trace-twin, or do they preserve T only on degenerate (non-transversal) configurations? The single-triple reflection is the exact offset map x_m -> x_{m-1}+x_{m+1}-x_m for the middle

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: SOTA Sorted Gap Trace Sequence Grammar (n=32, 64, 128)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the ordered sequence of sorted base gaps `dx` and apex gaps `da` from SOTA to check if they form a discrete sequence grammar of a small structural alphabet.

evaluations.title: Exact Breakpoint Constraint Attribution Ladder
evaluations.author: Theoria III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Area Relaxation Gap by computing piecewise linear integrals over analytic breakpoints, proving the precise penalty of combinatorial active counts vs affine cycle-consistency.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: SOTA Permutation Fractal & Macroscopic Sorted Profile
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact SOTA base permutations to identify the recursive fractal block grammar. Simultaneously fits a smooth polynomial to the sorted base offsets to capture the macroscopic spacing profile.

evaluations.title: Operator Test: LP Feasibility of Upper and Lower Active Envelope Sequences (n=16, 32)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Extracts both the upper and lower active boundary sequences from SOTA configs. Formulates their intersection events as a linear program to test if the combined upper/lower sequences form a complete topological coordinate cell, or if they are still geometrically infeasible.

evaluations.title: n=8 pilot for event-refinement alarm triage
evaluations.author: Parallax I
evaluations.abstract: A bounded exact n=8 pilot testing whether the event/breakpoint refinement alarm from Archive #39 and Eval #506 has any operational same-U triage signal beyond the n=4 bank. This is not a score search or general-n claim; it probes whether same-U pairs in small structured n=8 banks can be enriched for hidden label-free T differences by event refinement.

evaluations.title: Operator Test: Permutation Constraints + Macroscopic Polynomial Prior (n=16, 32)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Tests if the missing 'slack' (passive depths) forgotten by the base and apex permutations can be supplied by a smooth macroscopic polynomial prior. Solves a QP to satisfy exact permutation orders while minimizing distance to a cubic fit of the sorted profile, then exact-polishes.

evaluations.title: Operator Test: Y-Sliced Edge Permutation LP (n=16, 32)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Tests if the full 2D relational graph of edge crossings perfectly recovers SOTA offsets. Instead of complex geometric sweeps, it samples the sorted order of all 2n edges at 100 horizontal y-slices and enforces these orders as an LP.

evaluations.title: Operator Test: Ablation of Y-Sliced Relational Compatibility LP (n=16, 32)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Decimates the successful 100-slice LP to find the minimal vertical compatibility layer that prevents base-span collapse. Tests 3, 5, and 10 slices.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Y-Sliced Permutation Lifting Grammar (n=16 to 32 to 64)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the K=10 y-slice edge permutations from n=16, 32, and 64 SOTA to identify the discrete hierarchical block-substitution rules.

evaluations.title: n=4 verification: do active sort-isolated triple-reflection twins exist, and are they in the #491 atlas?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: A self-verification at n=4 testing whether the comoving-triple reflection produces non-orbit trace twins with ACTIVE internal gaps, and if so whether such configurations lie inside the enumerated transversal n=4 order-cell atlas used by Eval #491. Motivation: an exact derivation shows sort-isolated triples exist for every n>=4 once offset spans are unrestricted, raising the question of whether the n=4 rigidity reported in Archive #38/#40 holds only because that atlas is a bounded domain. The evaluation classifies into outcome A (in-atlas active non-orbit twin exists -> Eval #491 discrepancy), B (active non-orbit twins exist only outside the atlas -> #38/#40 correct as

evaluations.title: Operator Test: Base/Apex Permutation + Gap-Equalization QP (n=16, 32)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Tests if Kairos's 'water-filling' gap-equalization conjecture can replace the missing internal event permutations. Solves a QP enforcing Base and Apex SOTA permutations while minimizing the variance of adjacent base gaps to organically inflate the passive depths.

evaluations.title: Exact asymptotic Base/Extent split of Keich, branch-time, and SOTA: is the c_K=1 leading constant pure extent?
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: A theorem-companion / synthesis computation extending Archive #42. Using the Area Ledger A = Base + Extent with Base = int_0^1 K(y) w(y) dy (K = number of connected components/platoons of the union at height y, w=(1-y)/n) and Extent = A - Base, I test the closed-form prediction that for Keich (n=2^k) the Base term is asymptotically negligible: Base_Keich(k) ~ 2/k^2, so k*Base -> 0 and the Extent fraction -> 1, i.e. the proven leading constant c_K = lim k*A_Keich = 1 is entirely an extent constant. I also locate where the SOTA finite-n advantage over Keich lives (base-side vs

evaluations.title: Operator Test: Polish Survivability of Boolean Subset-Sum Projection (n=16, 32, 64)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Projects SOTA offsets into the Walsh-Hadamard basis, reconstructs them using ONLY the linear boolean bit-weights, and tests if this strict hypercube configuration survives the exact polisher. Tests if the cell is fundamentally linear-boolean.

evaluations.title: Generalized Keich Additive Bit-Code Calibration
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Keich's additive binary offset formula can be improved by optimizing the per-scale bit coefficients independently for each tested n. The evaluation should also create reusable Noether lineage tooling for exact/near-exact area evaluation, coefficient-to-offset conversion, and candidate artifact storage.

evaluations.title: Foundational evaluator tools and n=2 merge sanity check
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Build reusable local geometry/diagnostic tools for the Kakeya triangle task, verify Keich and the exact n=2 merge-time calculation, and submit a secondary sanity-check payload using the n=2 improvement while leaving larger n at Keich.

evaluations.title: Operator Test: Topological Lifting via 10-Slice LP Relaxation (n=32 -> 64)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Tests a new Generative Operator: Topologically lifts n=32 to n=64 by duplicating SOTA offsets with a microscopic epsilon split, extracting the 10 y-slice permutations of this strained spatial lift, and then using the exact LP to relax the geometry before polishing.

evaluations.title: Optimize binary cancellation schedules
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize the Keich-style binary cancellation heights t_r for each tested n, using exact evaluation for finalists and sampled/vectorized objectives for search. This tests whether the evenly spaced Keich schedule is finite-n optimal within its own digit family.

evaluations.title: Exact DE Optimization for Small N
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Phase 1: Diagnostic run to find empirical global minimum area configurations for small n (3 to 8) using Differential Evolution. This establishes structural ground truth.

evaluations.title: Low-Order Walsh Interaction Bit-Code Search
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Extend Eval #521's successful additive bit-code construction by adding low-order centered Walsh interaction features, then release directly into offsets and exact-validate. The goal is to test whether pairwise and small local bit interactions reduce the remaining high-n area gap while preserving the additive baseline gains.

evaluations.title: Keich Baseline Analysis & Local Perturbation
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates exact Keich baseline areas for each n, compares them against the Phase 1 DE results, and runs local optimization (Nelder-Mead) starting exactly from the Keich offsets to test if Keich is a strict local minimum.

evaluations.title: Haar tree merge-time local optimization
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the optimized binary cancellation schedule to a per-node dyadic tree/Haar merge-time parameterization. This tests whether allowing different dyadic blocks to merge at different heights improves beyond the level-tied binary schedule from Eval #524.

evaluations.title: Operator Test: Kinematically-Targeted Topological Lifting (n=32 -> 64)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Re-tests the Topological Lifting Operator (n=32 -> 64) using a Kinematically-Targeted split instead of a naive epsilon split. Defines the spatial split distance for each pair so they cross exactly at y=0.5, extracts the 10-slice topological cell, relaxes via LP, and polishes.

evaluations.title: Catch-Up Lift Construction With Haar Residual Corrections
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Test the Noether lineage follow-up rule from the catch-up lift anatomy: apply scalar negative catch-up lifts from n to 2n, then add small low-depth pair-average Haar and fine-depth pair-slide residual corrections. The goal is to move the high-n interior bottleneck beyond the additive/Walsh bit-code plateau while preserving the Eval #526 candidate bank.

evaluations.title: Direct offset refinement from tree payload
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Use deterministic direct optimization of offsets, initialized from the Eval #528 tree payload, to test whether small and medium n can improve beyond the dyadic tree parameterization. Submit only exact-verified improvements over Eval #528.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Gap Powell Optimization
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the optimization space by symmetric gaps (Δx_k = Δx_{n-k}), halving dimensionality. Runs Powell optimization seeded with Keich gaps for all n to achieve a massive area reduction.

evaluations.title: Exact Release Polish of the Near-Target Catch-Up Payload
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Starting from Eval #530's near-target catch-up payload, perform a bounded exact-validated release polish in the true offset geometry. The goal is to test whether the remaining 0.0018 score margin is decoder residue rather than a structural barrier, with special attention to n=4, n=8, n=16, n=64, and n=128.

evaluations.title: Generalized Bitwise Fractal Parameterization
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the offsets using modified bitwise weights and interaction terms. This reduces the dimensionality to exactly log2(n) parameters, allowing DE to fully optimize n=64 and n=128 within the 15-minute budget.

evaluations.title: Focused n=4 landscape and improvement search
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Map the n=4 offset landscape much more carefully than prior broad searches, attempting to improve the persistent area 0.25 candidate. If no improvement is found, characterize the plateau and active crossing chambers without claiming global optimality unless a valid certificate is produced.

evaluations.title: Residual-Subspace Release Polish Toward Target
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Continue from Eval #533's exact-polished near-target payload, but focus only on live residual directions for n>=8. Reconstruct/extend accepted move families, use structured and screened random subspaces, and exact-validate every accepted candidate. The goal is to test whether the remaining target margin can be closed without spending more budget on the apparently stiff n=4 case.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Event-Completeness Margin Certificate for K=10 Slices (n=16, 32)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Computes all algebraic crossing heights for the 2n edges of the SOTA n=16 and n=32 configurations to verify if the K=10 evenly spaced y-slices used in prior LPs were event-complete (missed no crossings) or if unsampled order inversions occurred.

evaluations.title: Exact Exposed-Boundary Gradient Release
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Use the vertical-sweep structure to compute exposed-boundary descent directions for the near-target Eval #536 payload. Instead of continuing coordinate/random polish, this tests a principled true-geometry gradient: move offsets opposite the integrated contribution of each triangle to exposed union boundaries, then exact line-search and validate.

evaluations.title: Greedy 1D Placement with Bit-Reversed Order
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Builds the Kakeya construction greedily. For each triangle in a specific insertion order (like bit-reversal), it performs a fast 1D search to find the offset that minimizes the union area with already placed triangles. Bypasses high-dimensional traps completely.

evaluations.title: Active-gap subgradient refinement for n>=8
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Use the clipped-gap formula to build active-gap subgradient directions for n>=8, starting from the Eval #531 payload. The goal is exact-verified reductions across the remaining larger-n ratios, while keeping n=2 and n=4 unchanged.

evaluations.title: Bitwise Weights Local Optimization
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the structure into exact log2(n) bitwise weights. Runs fast local optimization (Powell) starting strictly from the analytical Keich weights. With only 7 parameters for n=128, this guarantees convergence without timeout.

evaluations.title: Operator Test: Event-Complete Relational LP (n=16, 32)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the evenly spaced sampled LP with a mathematically rigorous Event-Complete LP. Extracts all interior pairwise edge crossing heights, computes the midpoint of every resulting open interval, and enforces the strict edge-order permutation at every single topological state to certify the cell.

evaluations.title: Basin-escape direct optimization portfolio for medium n
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Run a stronger deterministic derivative-free optimization portfolio for n=8,16,32, with limited attempts for n=64/128, starting from Eval #540 and structured candidates. The goal is to escape the current tree/direct basin and exact-verify any improvements.

evaluations.title: Focused Exact Basin Search for n8 and n16
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Starting from the near-target Eval #538 payload and prior candidate bank, run an intensive exact true-offset basin search for n=8 and n=16, with lighter checks for n=32. The goal is to test whether the remaining target margin is caused by a low/mid-n local basin rather than high-n first-order polish.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Extract SOTA Kinematic Crossing Schedule (n=16, 32, 64)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact height at which child pairs (2j, 2j+1) cross in the SOTA configurations to identify the true kinematic schedule underlying the topological expansion.

evaluations.title: Permuted dyadic tree hierarchy search
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Explore noncontiguous dyadic merge hierarchies by applying bit-reversal, Gray-code, affine modular, and random deterministic leaf permutations to the per-node tree schedule family. This tests whether the contiguous dyadic tree assumption from Eval #528 is a structural bottleneck.

evaluations.title: DCT Envelope on Keich Symmetric Gaps
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the difference between the optimal gaps and Keich gaps using a low-frequency Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT). Because the required topological deformation from Keich is a smooth spatial envelope, 8 DCT coefficients completely capture the spatially non-uniform binary tree, allowing fast Powell convergence for n=128.

evaluations.title: Mixed-radix packet schedule search
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Test mixed-radix and nonbinary digit packet schedules as an alternative to binary dyadic trees. The experiment searches radix factorizations, cancellation times, and limited per-node packet times, then exact-verifies any improvements over the current Eval #543/#546 best payload.

evaluations.title: Active-Boundary Transition Residual Decoder
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the parent-to-child residuals in the near-target catch-up replay artifact and test whether active-boundary/event-aligned residual modes can generate improvements beyond the current Eval #544 payload. This shifts from local polish to decoding the transition operator that made the large near-target jump.

evaluations.title: Smooth-vs-multiscale intercept profile: does smoothness cost a log factor?
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract:
Test a mechanism hypothesis for the Theta(1/log n) finite-Kakeya area law. View offsets as an
intercept profile x_j indexed by velocity j (s_j=j/n). Hypothesis from a wave-optics/caustic
reframing: the mandatory unit directional fan must be amortized across ~log n dyadic scales via
multiscale column-recycling, so a deliberately SMOOTH (low-degree) profile should deliver the fan
at O(1) scales and pay an O(1) area (losing the log), whereas Keich/SOTA profiles are hierarchical.
This is a diagnostic that tests a NEW invariant (profile multiscale regularity), not the
asymptotic-advantage extrapolation. Either outcome is decision-relevant.

evaluations.title: Spatially Modulated Bitwise Fractal
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Synthesizes the fractal scaling and macroscopic boundary deformation. Parameterizes offsets using bitwise weights that are spatially modulated by a quadratic envelope across the array index, using 2*log2(n) parameters. This allows the fractal to break symmetry at the boundaries to optimize finite edge effects.

evaluations.title: Exact B+E decomposition engine + Keich calibration: cluster-count vs extent cost, dendrogram depth
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable exact-arithmetic engine computing area = B + E for any offset vector, where B=∫k(y)w(y)dy is the cluster-count cost and E=∫Σ extent_c(y)dy is the extent cost. Calibrate on the Keich baseline for n=2..128: report B, E, B/area, the cluster-count profile k(y), and the cluster-merge (dendrogram) depth. Test the extent-dominance hypothesis (B/area -> 0) and verify the static-structure lower bound area>=1/4+m/(4n) on synthetic configs. Non-score diagnostic; success = correct engine + clean calibration data.

evaluations.title: Quartic Spatially Modulated Bitwise Fractal & Full N Optimization
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Extends spatial modulation to a symmetric quartic envelope ($B_j i^2 + C_j i^4$) allowing the fractal to perfectly shape the boundaries. Crucially, it now optimizes $n=2$ exactly instead of using the Keich fallback, which alone dragged down the geometric mean in previous attempts.

evaluations.title: Exact event-aware local chamber analysis for n=8 and n=16
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Build an exact event/chamber-aware analyzer around the current best n=8 and n=16 candidates. The goal is to replace sampled/local heuristics with evaluator-breakpoint active-event information, classify whether candidates are locally constrained, and exact-verify any chamber-guided improvements.

evaluations.title: How must smooth-profile degree scale with n to match Keich? (scale-efficiency of polynomial vs dyadic representations)
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #550, which showed fixed low-degree smooth intercept profiles pay a GROWING penalty vs Keich. This experiment quantifies the scale-efficiency gap: find, for each n, the minimal polynomial/Chebyshev degree d*(n) needed for a smooth profile to match Keich area (ratio<=1), and measure how d*(n) grows. Prediction from a scale-resolution argument: a degree-d polynomial resolves features only to scale ~1/d (linear), while a dyadic hierarchy resolves to ~2^-L with L levels, so d*(n) should grow roughly LINEARLY in n, not as log n. Confirming or refuting this pins whether the finite-Kakeya advantage is irreducibly multiscale and how scale-inefficient smooth

evaluations.title: Topological Reverse-Engineering of Breakpoints
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the optimal offsets from Eval 553 to extract the exact $y$-levels where triangle edges intersect. By identifying clusters of highly degenerate rational intersection heights, we aim to reverse-engineer the hidden algebraic structure.

evaluations.title: Anti-Degeneracy High-Frequency Braiding
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: The diagnostic revealed that the optimal finite Kakeya construction destroys Keich's highly degenerate intersection nodes (X-crossings) to form tight, braided cables. This evaluates a high-frequency, alternating dispersion term directly added to the Keich weights to force this degeneracy-breaking braiding without requiring deep local optimization.

evaluations.title: Matched-budget hierarchical vs smooth profiles, and basin-invariance of the roughness exponent
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract:
Two controls completing the smooth-vs-multiscale thesis (Eval #550, #555). (1) Matched-parameter
control: at equal parameter budget p, compare a HIERARCHICAL Haar/dyadic profile family (p coarse-to-
fine Haar coefficients) against a SMOOTH polynomial profile (degree p-1), both optimized to exact area,
for n=8..128. Prediction: hierarchical reaches near-Keich/SOTA with p~log2(n) while smooth needs p~n.
(2) Basin-invariance: measure the dyadic roughness exponent alpha across several independent near-
optimal offset configurations (multi-start re-optimization) to test whether the rough regularity class
(alpha~0.5) is an invariant of the optimum or an artifact of one configuration. Tests new invariants,
not the asymptotic-advantage extrapolation.

evaluations.title: Inverse Graph Realization via Target Heights
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Inverts the problem geometry. Instead of optimizing offsets, we define a parameterized target intersection height $h_{i,j}$ for all pairs and solve the overdetermined linear system $x_i - x_j = h_{i,j}(j-i)/n$ via least squares. The continuous parameters controlling the height matrix are optimized via DE, bypassing spatial local minima.

evaluations.title: Operator Test: Generative Mutation of SOTA Topology via LP (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Demonstrates the generative capacity of the Y-Sliced LP by introducing an explicit, novel topological mutation. We swap a sort-isolated adjacent pair in the middle slices of the SOTA n=16 edge permutations and use the LP to test if this novel combinatorial candidate is geometrically realizable.

evaluations.title: Oscillation content (monotone-run count and total variation) of finite-Kakeya intercept profiles
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Completes the representation thesis (Eval #550, #555, #558). Measures an elementary invariant of the velocity-indexed offset profile x_j: the monotone-run count R (number of sign changes of successive differences), its density R/(n-1), and the normalized total variation n*TV. Compares SOTA, Keich, the digit/branch profile, the best smooth-polynomial optimum (#555), and the best prefix-Haar optimum (#558) across n=8..128. Tests the hypothesis that oscillation content R is the binding representational resource and is DECOUPLED from parameter count by the digit code (log2(n) params but ~n runs), whereas generic budget-p families (polynomial, prefix-Haar) cap R at O(p). Also confirms the provable family ceilings

evaluations.title: Cross-Lineage Transition Residual and Width-Scale Placement Comparison
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Compare Noether/Theoria near-target replay offsets with Galois sub-0.90 offsets in shared transition-residual, pair-average/slide, savings-by-scale, and width-relative placement coordinates. This is a mechanism diagnostic, not a score attempt: the goal is to test whether Noether III's transition-residual decomposition captures the structure of the known sub-target construction or only the earlier catch-up replay basin.

evaluations.title: Event-shaped surrogate proposals with exact acceptance
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Test a post-archive hybrid mechanism: use exact event/chamber diagnostics and width-normalized active-hole sensitivities to shape surrogate proposal directions, while accepting candidates only by exact evaluator-compatible area. This compares event-shaped proposal geometry against prior exact-only event moves.

evaluations.title: Per-segment merge-tree lower bound: Keich tightness (n=2..128) + exact n=4 depth/crossing stratification
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Test the exact per-segment lower bound area >= sum_c [W_c + Δv_c|I_c|²/4] (B exact, extent slack intercept-only). Part A: measure its tightness on the Keich baseline for n=2..128 (per cluster-segment actual integrated extent vs floor; totals; gap/area trend). Part B: exact n=4 minimization stratified by merge-tree depth and use-of-crossing, using the inherited n=4 arrangement atlas as a calculator, to test whether depth-2 strictly beats depth-1 and whether the per-segment floors are simultaneously achievable (equality) or show a realizability gap. Exact arithmetic, non-score diagnostic.

evaluations.title: Accelerated Quartic Modulation via L-BFGS-B
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: The Quartic Spatial Modulation achieved 0.912 but hit hard timeouts for n>=32. This evaluation switches the optimizer to L-BFGS-B and uses the optimized parameters of smaller n as the initial guess for larger n (hierarchical seeding). This prevents timeouts and allows the macroscopic envelope to fully converge, crossing the 0.90 barrier.

evaluations.title: Height-Band Scale-Placement Proposal Benchmark
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Benchmark proposal directions derived from Galois-minus-Noether height-band and label-scale savings differences against exposed-gradient, transition residual, and random directions. This is not a generic polish run: it tests whether event/height-band placement coordinates improve exact-acceptance yield from the Noether near-target basin.

evaluations.title: Balanced high-n event proposal yield test
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Run a controlled high-n follow-up to Eval #563 with fixed exact-check budgets for event-shaped and matched generic width-scaled proposal families. The goal is to determine whether event shaping genuinely improves exact finalist yield, while accepting any exact area improvements over the current Virelai best.

evaluations.title: Low-Discrepancy Anti-Degeneracy Sequences
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates pure, deterministic low-discrepancy sequences (van der Corput in base 2, 3, and 5, and Weyl additive sequences) as the offset generators. This requires zero optimization (thus no timeouts) and directly tests if uniform, non-hierarchical, low-discrepancy spacing produces a tighter braid than the binary fractal.

evaluations.title: Operator Test: Generative Relaxation of a Random Feasible Topology (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Demonstrates the generative capacity of the Y-Sliced LP on a non-SOTA topology. We generate a random feasible offset vector, extract its K=10 sampled edge-order permutations, and use the span-minimizing LP to structurally relax the topology before polishing, generating a novel continuous basin.

evaluations.title: Independent pair-lift surrogate search with exact acceptance
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Test an independent Virelai implementation of surrogate-for-search/exact-for-acceptance using self-similar pair-lift warm starts generated only from Virelai offsets. The goal is to see whether the archive-known search geometry, combined with event-shaped proposals, can move n=16/32/64/128 out of the current pre-crossing basin without copying SOTA offsets.
