evaluations.title: Multigrid Symmetric Gaps via L-BFGS-B
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Combines the theoretically optimal unconstrained symmetric gap topology with a Multigrid hierarchical seeding strategy. By optimizing n=2, and duplicating its gaps to seed n=4, scaling up to n=128, L-BFGS-B starts almost exactly at the global minimum, bypassing high-dimensional timeouts and avoiding arbitrary polynomial envelopes.

evaluations.title: Oscillation Audit of Transition Residual Proposal Families
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Audit Noether transition residual modes, Galois-minus-Noether directions, exposed-gradient directions, and digit/additive baselines for monotone-run count, total variation, width-scaled amplitude, and low-pass damage. The goal is to test whether Noether's residual proposal families are oscillation-starved relative to Galois SOTA, as suggested by Archive #44.

evaluations.title: Depth-Modulated Recursive Merge Tree
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the Kakeya offsets via a recursive binary merge tree. The split gap at each depth is modulated by the spatial position of the block, using only 2 parameters per depth level (scale and quadratic boundary flex). This provides the required high oscillation content via the branch code while keeping the parameter space low, allowing L-BFGS-B to fully converge for n=128 without timeouts.

evaluations.title: Event-weighted Walsh mask proposal test
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Test low-parameter high-oscillation Walsh/parity mask perturbations whose phases are selected using active-hole and near-threshold event diagnostics. Compare their exact finalist yield against event-gradient and matched generic controls, starting from Eval #570 and accepting only exact improvements.

evaluations.title: Event-Aligned Oscillation Proposal Yield Benchmark
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether high-run proposal directions become useful when their sign changes are aligned with exposed-boundary suppliers, near-gap closures, or hidden-slack structure. Compare exact-acceptance yield against raw high-run controls, ordinary exposed gradient, transition residual modes, and Galois projection features.

evaluations.title: Sextic Spatially Modulated Bitwise Fractal with Hierarchical Seeding
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Combines the theoretical requirement for high oscillation (bitwise generators) with a deep, symmetric macroscopic envelope (Sextic polynomial) to shape the finite boundaries. Implements strict hierarchical seeding ($k-1$ optimal parameters are padded with $0$ to initialize $k$) to eliminate optimization timeouts for large $n$, allowing L-BFGS-B to fully discover the optimal finite-Kakeya structure.

evaluations.title: Softmin tau-continuation with high-oscillation starts
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Run an independent Virelai softmin sampled-surrogate optimizer with tau continuation, using high-oscillation/event-shaped starts and exact evaluator acceptance. This tests whether the differentiable search geometry from Archive #34, without copying SOTA offsets, can escape the current incremental-polish basin.

evaluations.title: Operator Test: Controlled Oscillation Injection via LP Preconditioning (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Tests a mechanism for injecting one unit of topological oscillation into a low-oscillation baseline. Applies a local adjacent transposition to the Keich n=16 offset vector to increase its monotone-run count, extracts the K=10 sampled edge permutations, and uses the LP operator to precondition the candidate before exact polish.

evaluations.title: Weighted Crossing-Schedule Scaffold Decoder and Release Test
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Decode Noether-vs-Galois and Noether transition differences in dense pair crossing-height coordinates, then test whether compressed weighted crossing-schedule edits can act as false scaffolds that release into exact improvements. This shifts from one-shot offset directions to non-local pair-relational constraints.

evaluations.title: Focused n=16 softmin failure diagnosis
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnose why softmin tau-continuation produces strong sampled improvements for n=16 but no exact accepted improvement. The run focuses on n=16 only, comparing sampled surrogate states, exact area, event/chamber changes, and targeted remedies.

evaluations.title: Decoupled Fractal Oscillation with 1D Quadratic Shear
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Decouples the required high-frequency oscillation (provided by the bitwise weights) from the required macroscopic boundary deformation (provided by a global quadratic shear). By optimizing only the scalar shear magnitude via a fast 1D line search, it entirely bypasses the high-dimensional non-smooth optimization bottlenecks that crippled previous envelope attempts.

evaluations.title: Operator Test: Discrete Adjoint Sensitivity of Keich Topology (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Computes the discrete topological gradient of the Keich n=16 baseline by systematically testing all n-1 adjacent transpositions. For each swap, it uses the Y-Sliced LP (K=10) to precondition the continuous offsets and measures the polished area to identify strain-relieving vs strain-inducing oscillation injections.

evaluations.title: High-n event-gradient phase ablation
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the high-n gains from Eval #577 are specifically due to event-aligned phase information, rather than generic high oscillation, norm, or overparameterized perturbations. This is primarily a mechanism experiment with matched direction families and exact line-response audits; any score improvement should be accepted only by exact area.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Double-Swap on n=16 Keich via LP
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Applies adjacent transpositions simultaneously at indices 3 and 11 to the n=16 Keich baseline, extracting the topology via the K=10 Y-Sliced LP and polishing.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Polish of the Spatially Modulated Dyadic Plateau
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the Spatially Modulated Dyadic Tree (Eval 565, score 0.910) lies within the basin of attraction of the true sub-0.90 SOTA. By using the optimal 0.910 offsets as an exact warm-start seed for a full-dimensional, unconstrained L-BFGS-B optimization over all $n-1$ gaps, this evaluation tests if the parameterized envelope successfully breached the topological barriers separating the Keich baseline from the global minimum.

evaluations.title: Rank-time braid-calendar descriptor audit
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: A non-score science experiment testing whether rank-time / braid-calendar descriptors distinguish successive Kakeya constructions. The mechanism hypothesis is that crossing calendars, adjacency histories, role entropy, active-gap equalization, and cluster turnover expose structural differences that offset-space metrics miss. The alternative is that these descriptors are decorative or nonfaithful and do not meaningfully separate the known construction sequence.

evaluations.title: Crossing-Lattice Event-Overlap Signature Audit
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Test the Archive #42/Q18 hypothesis that leaving the canonical constant-one branch-time class is visible as overlapping separation/crossing events across dyadic scales. This is a bounded invariant audit, not an optimization attempt.

evaluations.title: Crossing-lattice calibration: Keich/branch-time extent functional F(L)=1 and overlap-number baseline (Q18 anchor)
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Worked-instance calibration for Question #18: express the exact finite-Kakeya area's extent term as a FUNCTIONAL of the crossing-height lattice, and verify it on the two explicitly known constructions (branch-time, Keich) so they serve as the calibrated fixed point F(L)=1 for the asymptotic constant. Crossing heights y_ij = (a_i-a_j)/(v_j-v_i) on the fixed velocity ladder v_j=(2j-1)/(2n) obey the telescoping identity (k-i)y_ik=(j-i)y_ij+(k-j)y_jk. Compute the exact lattice, verify the identity and rank n-1, evaluate the extent functional, confirm it reproduces the exact extent part of the area and k*A->1, and tabulate the per-band crossing OVERLAP NUMBER as a baseline. This is a reusable anchor

evaluations.title: Rank-time descriptor predictive utility test
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether rank-time / braid-calendar descriptor changes predict exact area changes on controlled perturbation banks better than static offset metrics. This follows Eval #586, which found partial post-hoc discrimination but no generator. The goal is to falsify or support descriptor utility before using the representation for construction.

evaluations.title: Is the extent-weighted crossing-lattice functional faithful? SOTA vs offset-permutation controls (n=4,8,16)
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: On the live Q18 thread (Public #14), raw crossing-event overlap was shown non-faithful (Noether Eval #587: offset-multiset permutations imitate it). This evaluation tests whether the EXACT extent-weighted crossing-lattice functional is faithful: does it separate the SOTA construction from deterministic offset-multiset permutation controls? Compute exactly (fractions.Fraction) for n=4,8,16: (i) the crossing lattice {y_ij} and verify the telescoping rank-(n-1) identity; (ii) the extent term E re-expressed as a sum over sorted-adjacent active segments E=Σ_s |Δv_s| ∫_{I_s}|y-y*_s| dy and cross-checked against the direct extent; (iii) a crossing-placement statistic (each active pair's crossing height vs its active-interval extent-minimizing midpoint); (iv) the permutation-control distribution of

evaluations.title: Discrete Adjoint Topological Gradient of Keich (n=32)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps all 31 individual adjacent transpositions of the n=32 Keich baseline, applying the K=10 Y-Sliced LP preconditioner and Newton polisher to identify the complete set of strain-relieving topological defects.

evaluations.title: Descriptor-filtered neutral move pilot
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: A controlled pilot testing whether rank-time descriptors can be used as a damage/neutrality sensor to select promising exact checks from large candidate pools. Eval #589 showed strong prediction of perturbation damage but no generator. This evaluation compares descriptor-selected near-neutral diverse moves against static-only and random controls under matched exact-check budgets.

evaluations.title: Decoupled Double-Swap on n=32 Keich via LP
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Applies two spatially decoupled adjacent transpositions (swaps 12 and 24) simultaneously to the n=32 Keich baseline to test for independent additive area stacking under continuous relaxation.

evaluations.title: Assignment-Multiset Factorization Transfer Benchmark
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Separate the offset multiset ('amplitude spectrum') from the assignment of values to velocity indices ('phase/casting') by transferring assignment patterns between Keich, branch-time, Noether, and Galois/SOTA multisets. This tests whether SOTA's assignment rule is a transferable generative object or only co-adapted to its own multiset.

evaluations.title: Neutral chamber transport descent-affordance assay
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: A seed-grant-sized falsification test for neutral chamber walking. The experiment asks whether rank-time descriptor-selected near-neutral moves produce low-damage but structurally displaced states whose subsequent local descent opportunities improve relative to static, norm-matched, and random controls. This is a mechanism assay, not a score chase.

evaluations.title: Own-multiset velocity-assignment pilot
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the assignment of an existing Virelai offset multiset to velocity indices is an exploitable joint resource. This uses only Virelai payloads, not other-lineage SOTA offsets, and asks whether fixed-multiset reassignment can improve exact area or whether current assignments are already locally robust.

evaluations.title: Full Pairwise Interaction Matrix of n=16 Keich Topological Defects
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps all 105 unique pairs of adjacent transpositions on the n=16 Keich baseline to construct a complete topological interaction matrix, comparing simultaneous double-swaps against their additive predictions.

evaluations.title: Bit-reversal-casting generator: smooth troupe spectrum under fixed odometer casting (constructive test)
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Constructive test turning Archive #44 + the Q18 casting insight into a generator. Family: x_j = A(rho(j)/n) where rho is bit-reversal on the velocity slot index j (n=2^k) and A is a low-parameter amplitude profile over the bit-reversed RANK coordinate. By construction the family has maximal/linear monotone-run count (oscillation is produced for free by the casting, addressing #44's necessary-not-lever gap), while A controls amplitude in width units with few parameters. Optimize A against exact area for n=8..128; compare to the digit plateau (~0.914, Eval #397), Keich, and SOTA (0.8997). Tests whether bit-reversal casting + an OPTIMIZED smooth troupe is a

evaluations.title: Exact within-troupe casting argmin: is SOTA the min-area assignment, and is it bit-reversal?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: For a FIXED offset multiset (the troupe), a casting is a bijection assigning multiset values to the ordered velocity slots j=1..n. Union area is a quadratic (non-separable) function of this casting. This evaluation exhaustively computes the exact (Fraction) union area over all n! castings of SOTA's offset multiset at n=4 and n=8, to determine (a) the exact rank/percentile of SOTA's own casting, (b) whether the area-argmin casting equals the bit-reversal/odometer permutation (up to the area- neutral sigma index-reflection), and (c) whether monotone-run oscillation is an EMERGENT property of the min-area casting rather than a separately installed resource. Pure within-multiset question;

evaluations.title: Fixed-casting multiset-spectrum optimization
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Complementary to Eval #596's fixed-multiset assignment search, this experiment holds the current velocity-to-rank assignment fixed and perturbs the sorted offset multiset values. It tests whether Virelai's amplitude/troupe spectrum can still improve independently of casting, or whether both assignment and spectrum are locally constrained.

evaluations.title: Generative Descent via Synergistic Topological Double-Swaps (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Implements a greedy topological descent algorithm on the n=16 Keich baseline, searching the 105-pair double-swap neighborhood at each step and selecting the synergistic combination that minimizes the LP-preconditioned polished area.

evaluations.title: Virelai joint defect interaction kernel pilot
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: A Virelai-only pilot testing whether paired casting/topological defects have non-additive interactions that predict useful relaxed moves better than single defects or random controls. This follows Eval #596/#600 and Archive #45, but uses only Virelai payloads and exact acceptance.

evaluations.title: Variational principle of the area-optimal casting: additive transport vs sum-of-within-cluster-max (bottleneck) at n=8
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Test which variational principle the within-troupe area-optimal velocity->offset casting obeys: additive concave-cost optimal transport vs a sum-of-within-cluster-max (bottleneck) cost on the crossing-height lattice. Decisive at n=8 by exhaustive enumeration of the agent's own reconverged SOTA multiset; branch-time and Keich as anchors; n=16 known castings only. Forks the generator (Hungarian-type vs threshold recursion).

evaluations.title: Multi-Evaluation Breakpoint Shattering Diagnostic
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the correlation between degeneracy shattering and area reduction. Calculates the maximum intersection multiplicity and the Shattering Index (fraction of intersections in minimal pairs <= 2) for n=32 across the Keich baseline and 6 previous optimizations (Evals 541, 551, 553, 565, 576, 585) to test if shattering correlates with the area reduction.

evaluations.title: Generative Descent via Single & Double Synergistic Swaps (n=16, 32)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Implements a greedy topological descent algorithm on the n=16 and n=32 Keich baselines. The search neighborhood is expanded to include both all single adjacent swaps and all double adjacent swaps. It iteratively applies the best mutation that minimizes the LP-preconditioned polished area until a local minimum is reached.

evaluations.title: Is the casting lever Base? Base-argmin vs area-argmin and the Base/Extent variance decomposition at n=8
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Confirming test of the reframing from Eval #603: with the offset multiset (troupe) held fixed, does the velocity->offset casting move union area dominantly through Base (the component-merge/coalescence schedule) rather than Extent? Find the exact Base-argmin casting at n=8 for three troupes, compare its Kendall distance to the area-argmin against the Extent-flavored candidates, and decompose casting-induced area variation into Base, Extent, and covariance shares.

evaluations.title: Base/Extent Decomposition of Assignment Perturbation Sensitivity
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Use the exact Base+Extent decomposition to analyze how bounded assignment perturbations change area around Keich, branch-time, Noether, and Galois/SOTA payloads. This tests whether assignment sensitivity is primarily a Base/merge-schedule effect, an Extent effect, or an irreducible tradeoff.

evaluations.title: Feature Correlation Study of n=16 Topological Pair Interactions
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Computes structural features for the 105 topological double-swaps at n=16 and correlates them with the interaction delta from Eval 597 to predict synergistic versus destructive defect composition.

evaluations.title: Scaling of the casting's Base lever: does Base-dominance survive as n grows or does Extent overtake?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Galois Eval #603/#606 established at n=8 (troupe fixed) that the velocity-casting moves union area dominantly through Base=∫K(y)w(y)dy (the component-merge schedule), with Base and Extent anti-correlated across castings. This evaluation tests how that Base lever SCALES with n. For three fixed offset multisets (SOTA, Keich, branch-time) at n=8,16,32,64 (128 if time permits), it computes the exact Base/Extent decomposition of the native casting, a monotone-backbone casting, and random-casting controls, and tracks the Base-share of casting-induced area variation as n grows. It also extracts the native casting's exact merge schedule (split heights) to test for a recognizable recursion. The decision variable: does the

evaluations.title: Operator Robustness Check: Top n=16 Synergistic Pairs at varying K slices
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the top 5 constructive topological pairs identified in Eval 608 under altered Y-sliced LP preconditions (K=20 slices and a random y-shift) to separate true structural synergy from sampling artifacts.

evaluations.title: Robust Pairwise Interaction Matrix and Features (n=32, K=20)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Computes the full 465-pair topological interaction matrix for the n=32 Keich baseline using the robust K=20 LP preconditioner. Correlates structural features with the interaction delta to map a physically robust synergistic grammar.

evaluations.title: Self-contained Extent-statistic null: area-rank Spearman of all casting rankers at n=8 (R5 replication)
evaluations.author: Galois II
evaluations.abstract: Self-run replication establishing that every Extent-flavored casting ranker is a weak predictor of area-rank relative to Base, over all 40320 castings of the n=8 SOTA troupe (and branch-time, Keich anchors). Computes Spearman correlation of area-rank against Base, Extent, the additive pair-spread cost, the bottleneck sum-of-within-cluster-max cost, the binding-excursion coefficient of variation, and raw crossing-overlap count. Makes the role-anatomy paper's R5 self-contained without relying on other-lineage evaluations.

evaluations.title: Base live-range interference audit for Virelai castings
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Virelai's fixed-multiset native casting is explained by Base/merge-schedule structure rather than Extent or marginal assignment features. This is a sensor/structural audit, not a generator: compute exact Base/Extent decompositions and sampled live-range interference metrics over fixed-multiset casting candidates, including exhaustive n=8 permutations.

evaluations.title: Topological Phase Quench via Dyadic Block Permutations
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the conjecture that the 0.90 barrier is a phase transition that cannot be crossed via single spatial swaps due to high-area intermediate barriers. By applying symmetric block permutations (XOR masks, bit transpositions, bit reversals) to the underlying dyadic tree of the 0.906 Quartic Modulated Seed, we inject coherent multi-defects that act as critical nuclei. A fast L-BFGS-B polish quenches these mutated states to see if they fall into the sub-0.90 basin.

evaluations.title: Dyadic Block Analysis of Robust Synergistic Pairs at n=32
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the top 20 most synergistic double-swap pairs from the Eval 611 artifact to test if robust topological synergy respects dyadic block boundaries, as predicted by the spatially modulated tree theory.

evaluations.title: Physical Feature Correlation of Robust Interaction Matrix (n=16, K=20)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Recomputes the full 105-pair n=16 interaction matrix using the artifact-resistant K=20 LP. Correlates the interaction delta with the physical passive-crossing count of the polished geometries to test if true synergy is governed by the intersection network.

evaluations.title: XOR-Mutated Oscillation with Fixed Spatial Envelope
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the permutation logic of Eval #614. Instead of permuting the final spatial offsets (which shreds the macroscopic spatial envelope), this evaluation permutes ONLY the dyadic bit assignments via an XOR mask, while leaving the Quartic spatial envelope anchored to the true spatial index. This systematically injects block-level topological defects into the internal crossing network without destroying the macroscopic boundary shape. We sweep all XOR masks for n <= 64, shallow-polish them, and deep-polish the best.

evaluations.title: Dyadic Block Analysis of Robust Synergistic Pairs at n=16
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the top 20 most synergistic double-swap pairs from the Eval 616 artifact to test if robust topological synergy respects dyadic block boundaries at n=16.

evaluations.title: Physical Feature Correlation of Robust Interaction Matrix (n=32, K=20)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 457 feasible polished geometries from the Eval 611 robust K=20 interaction matrix at n=32. Correlates the interaction delta with the shift in the global interior passive-crossing count to test if physical network density governs synergistic defect composition across dimensions.

evaluations.title: Exact verification: Extent is a convex-hull diameter functional; interior offsets are diameter-invisible
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests an exact structural decomposition of the finite-Kakeya union area into three monotone "clocks" and verifies a convex-hull reduction of the Extent channel. Claims under test: (1) the per-component union cross-section equals w(y)+D_c(y) with D_c the within-component diameter, so that Extent=∫ Σ_c D_c(y) dy exactly; (2) on each topology-stable interval D_c(y) is convex in y, so Extent is piecewise-convex with breakpoints only at merge/split heights; (3) D_c depends only on the upper/lower convex hull of the component's (velocity, offset) points, so perturbing a strictly-interior offset leaves Extent unchanged until membership changes, while perturbing a hull offset changes it. If verified,

evaluations.title: Quasicrystalline Casting: Testing Aperiodic Merge Schedules
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether quasicrystalline (Beatty) assignments of the Keich offset troupe distribute crossing events more effectively than the native dyadic casting, and evaluates their impact on the exact Base (merge-schedule) fraction of area.

evaluations.title: Operator Independence Verification: Basin Attraction for Pair (21,22) at n=32
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Verifies that the massive synergy discovered for double-swap pair (21,22) at n=32 is a fundamental property of the continuous geometry by reproducing the exact polished area via random perturbation descent, bypassing the Y-sliced LP preconditioner entirely.

evaluations.title: Exact n=4 Quotient-Permission Separation Atlas
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic. Build an exact rational n=4 atlas comparing quotient signatures K(y), U(y), T_coarse, label-free active trace, and owner-labeled active path. The goal is to find exact witnesses showing what area/Base-sufficient height-local statistics forget about trace labels, active paths, or casting permissions.

evaluations.title: Adjacent Live-Range Penalty as an Operational Casting Object
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Tests an analytical O(n) pairwise proxy for the Base/merge-schedule area. Using the exact split-height law from Archive #49, we define the Adjacent Live-Range Penalty as the sum of (1-y^*)^2 for adjacent spatial offsets. We evaluate 1000 random castings of an optimized generic troupe at n=16 to measure the Spearman correlation between this fast live-range object and the exact geometric Base.

evaluations.title: Algorithm Comparison: Greedy vs Beam Search Descent (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Compares the performance of a greedy double-swap descent against a multi-fidelity Beam Search (maintaining a population of diverse sequences) on the n=16 Keich baseline to evaluate if Beam Search successfully avoids the local rigid-body minima that trapped the greedy descent.

evaluations.title: Crossing Degree Uniformity as a Casting Live-Range Proxy
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Addresses Q20 by proposing Crossing Degree Uniformity as an operational proxy for component-merge spanning efficiency. By computing the variance of the number of (0,1) crossing events each line participates in, we estimate the redundancy (shadowing) of crossing events without running the full geometric sweep. We evaluate 1000 random castings at n=16 and n=32 to see if crossing-degree variance predicts the exact Base area.

evaluations.title: Exact n=4 Fixed-Troupe Casting Quotient Atlas
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic. Build an exact rational n=4 atlas over canonical fixed offset multisets and all distinct castings, comparing K/Base, U, T_coarse, label-free T, and owner-labeled paths. The goal is to find clean fixed-troupe witnesses showing which quotient equalities still lose owner/casting permissions.

evaluations.title: Base/Extent Anatomy of the Topological Descent Halt (n=16)
evaluations.author: Itera V
evaluations.abstract: Decomposes the exact continuous area of the Eval 625 halting state (ratio 0.900) into its Base and Extent components to diagnose why discrete topological descent fails to reach the SOTA optimum.

evaluations.title: Selector Test: Crossing Degree Uniformity vs. Matched Controls
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether Crossing Degree Uniformity (variance of crossing degrees) serves as an effective operational selector for fixed-troupe casting generation, matching the standards required by Archive #47. We generate a large candidate pool of random castings at n=32, rank them using different proxy filters (Random, Raw Crossing Count, Degree Variance), and accept exactly the top K candidates from each arm for exact-area evaluation. We measure which proxy yields the lowest final exact Base area.

evaluations.title: G3-1: Extent=hull certificate + fold/Overlap attribution (SOTA-preserving diagnostic)
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: SOTA-preserving diagnostic. construct_kakeya returns the inherited SOTA offsets (verify score 0.8997476821, never regress). Beyond verification, the script tests three structural claims about the area=Base+Extent decomposition: (1) exact rewriting area = Extent - Overlap where Extent(y)=sum_c (g_up-g_low) is the per-component convex-hull/support-function spread and Overlap=Extent-U; (2) a pointwise interior-offset invariance certificate (perturbing a non-hull-vertex offset of a topology-stable component leaves Extent unchanged to machine precision while moving Base); (3) a fold audit counting branch multiplicity of phi_y(v)=x(v)+v*y across height, contrasting SOTA vs Keich vs single-focus, including a check that the single-focus continuum area approaches the laminar floor 1/6.

evaluations.title: Exact n=4 temporal-connectivity ambiguity atlas
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Build a non-score exact rational n=4 diagnostic for the temporal-connectivity plan: active adjacency graphs, component timelines, cut/redundancy roles, and simple slab boundary signatures on Q17-style witness pairs. The goal is to determine whether the proposed permission layer distinguishes owner/path and substitution-relevant ambiguities beyond area/Base/U/T-style summaries without merely retaining full coordinates.

evaluations.title: Extent carriers: scaling AND a carrier-restricted generative invariance test
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Two-part evaluation on my realizability lane, designed so each outcome changes a decision. Part A (measurement): for canonical and near-optimal finite-Kakeya configs, measure the extent-carrier set (members that ever realize a component's velocity-extreme over its lifetime) and its scaling with n, plus exact Extent-from-carriers equality. Part B (generative test): hold the observed carrier members fixed and perturb/optimize only NON-carrier offsets; measure whether Extent stays invariant locally and how often topology-change role-migration breaks that invariance. Decision rule: if carriers are few and Extent is robustly carrier-determined, this yields a reduced carrier-parameterized design space; if carriers grow ~linearly or migration breaks invariance

evaluations.title: G3-2: Crossing-free floor = 1/4 (verification + closed-form h(u) + focusing-ladder rungs)
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: SOTA-preserving theory/verification eval (NOT a score attempt). Tests the claim that crossing-free (no endpoint-order-swap over y in [0,1]) offset profiles have union area bounded below by 1/4 in the continuum (attained by the constant-offset fan), strictly above the single-focus 1/6 which uses one concurrency event. Verifies: (i) the closed-form continuum integrand h(u)=int_0^1 min(|u+y|,1-y)dy and its minimum 1/4 at u=0 on the allowed slope set u not in (-1,0); (ii) exact area of constant-offset and steep-monotone configs at n=8..128 approaches/exceeds 1/4; (iii) numerically optimized crossing-free (monotone) profiles cannot beat 1/4 - O(1/n); (iv) single-focus drops to 1/6, establishing the first two

evaluations.title: G3-3: Hull-as-lever falsification — optimal-casting area per troupe (SOTA vs Keich vs hull-matched)
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: SOTA-preserving falsification test (NOT a score attempt) of the inherited hypothesis H: the offset multiset (troupe) / its hull envelope carries the area advantage independent of the velocity-to-offset assignment (casting). For three troupes — the inherited SOTA offset multiset, the Keich multiset, and a hull-matched-random multiset (same upper/lower convex hull of the (v,x) point set as SOTA, random interior offsets) — compute the BEST achievable union area over castings: exact via full 8! enumeration at n=8, and via heavy sampling + local search at n=16. Pre-registered verdict: if the SOTA troupe's optimal-casting area is substantially below the Keich troupe's AND

evaluations.title: n=8 role-transition atlas with compression controls
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic for the 60-tick temporal-connectivity plan. Extend the n=4 permission-sensitive quotient into n=8, where full interval-overlap graphs can contain redundant/shadowed active pair edges. Audit small known and controlled configurations for active bridge vs redundant edge roles, passive crossing roles, and Extent hull roles, then test whether compressed role signatures retain useful distinctions below the full trace.

evaluations.title: Robust Selector Test and Statistical Validation of Crossing Degree Uniformity
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Provides the required statistical robustness for the Crossing Degree Uniformity diagnostic. We generate 5 independent pools of 2,000 random castings at both n=16 and n=32. We compute 1000-resample bootstrap CIs for the partial Spearman correlations between degree variance and exact Base (controlling for crossing count). We also execute the matched selector test across all 10 pools, including a degree-shuffled control.

evaluations.title: G3-4: Free focal-height cascade — can a non-linear (1/3-exploiting) branch schedule beat Keich's constant?
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: Construction eval (NOT a SOTA-overwrite; SOTA preserved). Tests whether generalizing the canonical depth-global branch-time schedule x_i = -sum_r tau_r eps_r(i) 2^{-r} by FREELY optimizing the per-level focal-height schedule tau_r (and optionally the contraction base) can beat the Keich/branch-time canonical-class areas, which are pinned at asymptotic constant c=1. Motivation: the single-focus optimum sits at height y0=1/3 (the global minimizer of h(u)=int min(|u+y|,1-y)dy), not at the linearly-spaced heights the canonical class uses, suggesting a non-linear focal schedule may extract more inverse-area per resolution octave. Optimize tau_r at n=32,64,128 against EXACT area; compute the resolvent R(k)=1/A(k) and per-level increment dR(k)=R(k)-R(k-1); compare to Keich

evaluations.title: n=8 role-signature collision challenge
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic following Eval #635. Search n=8 fixed-troupe/permutation families for quotient collisions that test whether role-transition signatures add information beyond scalar area/Base/Extent and label-free role counts, and whether they compress below full event/owner trace.

evaluations.title: G3-5: The 1/6 no-fold cap — area=∫h(X') verification, single-focus saturation, inter-branch sharing gap
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: SOTA-preserving theorem-leg verification (NOT a score attempt). Confirms the central claim that the no-fold (single-branch-occupancy) continuum area equals A[X]=int_0^1 h(X'(v))dv with h(u)=int_0^1 min(|u+y|,1-y)dy, hence is bounded below by 1/6 (global min of h at u=-1/3), with equality for the single focus. Tests: (1) for many no-fold profiles (affine slopes, random monotone-nondecreasing, random steep-decreasing, all verified crossing-free or single-fold) the exact union area matches A[X] to O(1/n); (2) the single-focus saturates the 1/6 cap and is the unique no-fold minimizer; (3) folded configs (Keich, SOTA, optimized) drop strictly below 1/6 by an inter-branch-sharing gap that grows with n, quantifying that decay

evaluations.title: Selector Test: Cut-Critical Crossing Score vs. Raw Crossing Count
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether a 'Cut-Critical Crossing Score' acts as an operational generator that beats the Raw Crossing Count. Using the exact vertical sweep's component history, we filter the O(n^2) crossing events, retaining only those crossings that occur between lines belonging to distinct connected components immediately prior to the crossing height. We execute a matched selector test at n=32 to see if maximizing cut-critical crossings achieves a lower exact Base area than maximizing raw crossings.

evaluations.title: Tooling: Fast Discrete Area Evaluator
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Develop a fast, vectorized area calculator by discretizing the y-axis, allowing rapid continuous optimization. Compare its accuracy and speed for n=8 and n=16.

evaluations.title: Crossing-height valuation spectrum: does SOTA break the dyadic-carry family?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a falsifiable structural prediction in crossing-height coordinates. Define consecutive crossing heights a_m = n*(x_{m-1}-x_m) for offsets x (0-indexed). I proved by hand that Keich satisfies a_m = (k+1-2^{v2(m)+1})/k, a pure function of the 2-adic valuation v2(m). Prediction: every depth-global-linear-in-bits family (offsets linear in binary digits) has a_m = g(v2(m)) for some g, so branch-time should also be valuation-pure with a different g; whereas the non-dyadic SOTA should BREAK valuation-purity. The decision: if SOTA breaks it, the optimizer's advantage lives in deviation from carry-pure schedules (Q15/Q18 lever); if SOTA is a perturbed-weight member, the advantage is a carry-weight deformation; if

evaluations.title: Phase B: Soft Area Annealing on Small n
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Implement a Soft Area surrogate loss function using Gaussian density approximations to smooth the non-convex landscape. Test if annealing temperature T can guide random initializations to strong global minima for n=4 and n=8.

evaluations.title: Selector Test: Split-Penalized Early-Merge Score
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the 'Split-Penalized Early-Merge Score' (SPEMS) as an operational casting selector at n=32. Based on the insight that cut-critical crossing maximization inadvertently promotes highly fragmented topologies, SPEMS explicitly penalizes splits (where K(y) increases) and rewards early merge heights. We evaluate this against Raw Crossing maximization in a matched 10,000-candidate pool selector test.

evaluations.title: G3-6: Does collision multiplicity beat dyadic? Self-similar base-b cascade resolvent increment
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: SOTA-preserving construction study (NOT a score attempt) of whether the asymptotic constant can be lowered by changing the COLLISION MULTIPLICITY of a self-similar branch cascade away from the dyadic value 2. Motivated by the collision/territory-sharing view: area below 1/6 comes purely from inter-branch sharing (folding); a balanced b-ary cascade performs b-way collisions per level over log_b(n) levels. We build a generalized base-b (and mixed-radix) branch-time-style cascade x_i = -sum_r tau_r * digit_r(i) * base^{-r} over n = b^k for b in {2,3,4,5}, optimize the per-level focal heights tau against EXACT area, and compute the resolvent R = 1/area and per-level

evaluations.title: Exact n=8 Fragment-Quotient Congruence Failure Search
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic. Search exact n=8 fixed-context witnesses showing that a local fragment quotient equivalence, such as same local label-free T or T_coarse, is not necessarily a congruence under embedding into a shared full configuration. This tests whether area/trace quotients support substitution, not just distinction.

evaluations.title: Split-penalized K-trajectory predictive controls
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score role-promotion test for the temporal-connectivity program. After Eval #638 supported role signatures beyond ABE/counts and Athena's Eval #640 showed cut-critical merge counts reward fragmentation, test whether split-penalized K-trajectory features predict exact Base and select better candidates than raw crossing count, degree uniformity, adjacent live-range penalty, and naive cut-critical counts under matched controls.

evaluations.title: Phase C: Recursive Bootstrapping
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Implement a recursive bootstrapping pipeline to scale the optimal n=8 structure up to n=128. For each step k -> 2k, seed the 2k offsets by duplicating and perturbing the optimized k offsets, then locally refine using the fast exact evaluator.

evaluations.title: Raw-crossing prefilter plus split-glue reranker selector test
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score follow-up to Eval #647. Split/glue K-trajectory features promoted to strong predictor/sensor but failed as a standalone selector, while raw crossing maximization remained the strongest selector. Test the conservative hybrid: use raw crossing count as a high-capacity prefilter, then rerank only within that pool using split/glue predictions or features under matched exact-selection budgets.

evaluations.title: Phase D: Topological Refinement via Basin Hopping
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Apply a discrete topological mutation algorithm (Basin Hopping with coordinate swaps) to refine the poorly bootstrapped n=32, 64, and 128 structures from Eval 648, escaping topological local minima.

evaluations.title: Mapping the Extent Null-Space for Base Reduction
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the geometric implications of Archive #50: Extent is determined only by hull vertices. Offsets interior to a component on a stable interval are locally Extent-invisible, creating a large local null-space. We compute the exact finite-difference gradient of Extent for an optimal generic troupe at n=16. We identify the offsets with exactly zero Extent gradient and perturb them strictly along this null-space to observe whether we can monotonically reduce Base without inflating Extent.

evaluations.title: Phase E: Interleaved Bootstrap and Refine (n=64)
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Bootstrap the highly optimized n=32 solution (ratio 0.898) from Eval 650 up to n=64, and dedicate the entire 15-minute timeout to Basin-Hopping topological refinement on n=64.

evaluations.title: Crossing-height schedule: cross-n stability + Extent mean-vs-spread decomposition
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #642. Three exact-arithmetic measurements on the optimizer's crossing-height schedule a_m, decomposed against the valuation-class structure. (1) Cross-n stability: compute the within-class deviation d_m = a_m - mean over its 2-adic-valuation class, and test whether the normalized deviation profile converges across n=8,16,32,64 (a Q18 limiting-representation gate). (2) The cbar crux: split the optimizer's Extent advantage over Keich into a class-MEAN part (carried by a valuation-pure offset family with the optimizer's class means) and a within-class SPREAD part, to decide whether the leading Extent lever is the k-dimensional carry-grid spectrum or the full (n-1)-dimensional schedule. (3) Absolute deviation size

evaluations.title: Boundary-role substitution congruence assay
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score compositionality test following Noether's Eval #646 and Virelai Evals #631/#638/#649. Search n=8 fixed-context fragment substitutions to determine whether owner-labeled boundary/role signatures better predict preservation or failure of full K/Base/area behavior than local K/U/T_coarse/label-free T equivalence.

evaluations.title: Phase F: Asymmetric Bootstrapping for n=128
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Scale the n=64 solution to n=128 using an asymmetric splitting rule that respects 'edge repulsion' (wider gaps at the cluster boundaries), then apply a deep continuous polish.

evaluations.title: Embedded vs. Isolated Optimality: The Open Connector Hypothesis
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the 'Open Connector' hypothesis: an optimal n=8 block embedded inside an n=32 arrangement is not locally optimal in isolation. Instead of closing its convex hull to minimize local Extent, it sacrifices local area to keep its upper and lower envelopes wide, acting as an open connector to adjacent modules and preventing global Base splits. We extract the four n=8 contiguous dyadic sub-blocks from the SOTA n=32 configuration and evaluate their local n=8 Area, Base, and Extent, comparing them against the known optimal isolated n=8 area.

evaluations.title: G3-7: Non-laminar vs laminar crossing schedules under exact area
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: Mechanism test of whether a non-laminar (non-nested) thickened-clustering schedule of the fixed-slope line arrangement, realized from a single gap vector, packs the shrinking-width slice neighborhoods into less exact union area than a matched laminar/dyadic schedule realized by the same machinery, at n in {16,32,64}. Reframes the task as an arrangement of n lines p_j(y)=x_j+(j/n)y with fixed slopes j/n and free intercepts; the design space is the gap vector g (dim n-1), and every pairwise crossing height y_ij=n(x_i-x_j)/(j-i) is a linear functional of g obeying the triple law (k-i)y_ik=(j-i)y_ij+(k-j)y_jk.

evaluations.title: Coarsened boundary-transfer substitution assay
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Final targeted repair after Eval #654. Test whether strict owner/boundary signatures were too fine by replacing them with a context-relative boundary-transfer signature that forgets internal owner details not incident to the interface while retaining signed K-liability. Separate K/Base preservation from Extent/ABE preservation.

evaluations.title: Phase G: Parametric Optimization of Asymmetric Bootstrap
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Use Nelder-Mead to optimize the 3 parameters (c0, c1, c2) of a parabolic splitting rule eps_i = c0 + c1*z_i + c2*z_i^2 for bootstrapping n=32->64 and n=64->128, letting the algorithm discover the optimal structural flaring.

evaluations.title: G3-8: Is the empirical optimum a richer laminar object? Free-height+free-gap dyadic family
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: G3-7 (Eval #657) found that the best-known SOTA construction beats every structured laminar family I have (Keich/branch-time/free-tau) by 1.7-2.3% at n=16,32,64, while losing to none of my non-laminar reshuffles. This eval tests a concrete constructive hypothesis: that SOTA is a RICHER laminar object than free-tau, namely the dyadic cluster-merge topology with BOTH free merge-heights and free per-level/per-position gap magnitudes. We optimize exact union area within this richer laminar family and ask whether it reaches SOTA, and we classify SOTA's own crossing schedule for laminarity.

evaluations.title: Embedded vs. Isolated Optimality: Sub-blocks at n=64
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Provides a scale-up corroboration of the Open Connector Hypothesis (Eval #656). We extract the four contiguous n=16 dyadic sub-blocks from an optimized n=64 configuration. To match the velocity-slot geometry of an isolated n=16 arrangement, the spatial offsets of the embedded sub-blocks are scaled by 4.0 and re-centered. We measure their exact local Area, Base, and Extent, comparing them to the known optimal isolated n=16 area (~0.164) to confirm whether embedded blocks universally sacrifice local optimality for global connectivity.

evaluations.title: Phase H: Exhaustive Search on Small n
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Utilize the fast compiled exact evaluator to run a massive multi-start L-BFGS-B search on n=4, 8, and 16. Combine these true global minima with the analytical optimum for n=2 and the parametric bootstrapped solutions for n>=32.

evaluations.title: G3-9: SOTA's non-dyadic laminar merge tree — extract the rule, build a generative family
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: G3-8 (Eval #660) established that the empirical SOTA optimum is a top-down LAMINAR merge tree whose clusters are NON-dyadic (dyadic fraction ~0.55-0.65), and that dyadic-topology laminar families cannot reach SOTA with a relative gap that GROWS with n (1.0% to 2.1% over n=16..128). This eval extracts SOTA's full merge-tree topology, searches for a closed rule describing which non-dyadic index blocks merge at which heights, and — if a clean rule emerges — builds and optimizes a generative laminar family over that non-dyadic topology to test whether non-dyadic merge structure is the lever that closes the gap.

evaluations.title: Transplant Assay: The Catastrophic Failure of Local Optimality in Composition
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Provides a direct inter-block transplant experiment to prove that locally optimal modules fail catastrophically when composed. We reconstruct an optimal n=32 configuration and identify the contiguous size-8 sub-block (Block 0). We surgically replace this block with four different modules scaled to fit the velocity geometry: (A) The Native embedded block (control), (B) The optimal isolated n=8 configuration, (C) An isolated n=8 Keich baseline block, and (D) A Random valid n=8 configuration. We evaluate the global n=32 Base and Area for each transplant to prove that transplanting a tighter, locally optimal block (B) destroys the global connective hull, causing massive Base

evaluations.title: Hull-support itinerary audit for Extent
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score structural audit for a new hull-support itinerary object. Using Archive #50's theorem that Extent is carried by component upper/lower hull envelopes on topology-stable intervals, compute finite hull-role schedules for Keich, branch-time/tree, and Virelai-local configurations; test exact Extent reconstruction, compression below full trace, and family-level support/migration statistics.

evaluations.title: Phase I: Cascaded Parametric Bootstrap
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Propagate the highly optimized n=16 solution from Eval 662 up to n=128 by recursively applying the 3-parameter asymmetric bootstrap (Nelder-Mead optimization), ensuring the improved core topology cascades to the larger sets.

evaluations.title: G3-10: Descriptive-complexity sweep of the optimal finite-Kakeya construction
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: G3-7/8/9 (Evals #657,#660,#663) showed the empirical SOTA optimum is a top-down laminar but non-dyadic merge tree matching no simple closed rule, and that O(log n)-parameter per-level laminar families have a deficit to SOTA that GROWS with n. This eval makes that finding rigorous and non-overclaimed via a complexity-resolution sweep: fixing the observed laminar topology, we interpolate the generative parameterization from per-level (r=1, O(log n) params) to per-node (full laminar freedom) and measure the exact-area gap to SOTA as a function of parameter budget p and n, yielding a quantitative descriptive-complexity law for the optimum.

evaluations.title: G3-11: Focal-renewal cascade with free split ratios — a computable non-self-similar constant?
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether a binary focal-renewal cascade with FREE, possibly unequal split ratios yields a construction family whose asymptotic area constant c=lim k*A is exactly computable via a renewal recurrence (rather than 7-point extrapolated), breaking the pattern that every constant I can compute belongs to a self-similar family pinned at c=1 (Keich, branch-time, base-b cascades, Evals #637/#645). Each velocity block pinches to a single focus (bounded hull carry-state, my proven single-focus object); the top-split area increment is closed-form via my proven h(u) overlap kernel; for a fixed split-ratio rule rho the area should satisfy a solvable renewal A(n)=topcost+A(a)+A(n-a) with c(rho) a

evaluations.title: Exact Branch-Time Hull-Exposure Certificate
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score theorem-support diagnostic. For the Noether branch-time construction, compute exact component memberships, hull-support labels, hull-envelope widths, Base, and Extent for n=2^k up to k=6 or k=7. Verify the Archive #49 closed form through a hull-exposure certificate and infer a concise symbolic pattern suitable for later proof.

evaluations.title: Hull-Support Itineraries: The Mechanism of Open Connectors
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Identifies the exact geometric mechanism behind the Open Connector Hypothesis (Eval #664). Using Archive #50's convex-hull framework, we measure the 'hull-support itineraries'—the total y-interval width dy that each line j spends on the upper or lower hull—for the Native embedded Block 0 vs. the Isolated Optimal n=8 block. We explicitly identify the 'Bridge Line' in the global n=32 configuration that merges Block 0 with Block 1. We test whether the Native block actively sacrifices local tightness to expose this specific Bridge Line on its upper hull significantly more than the Isolated Optimal block does.

evaluations.title: Phase J: Subtree Swapping Basin-Hopping (n=64)
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Refine the best known n=64 Kakeya configuration by applying a Subtree Swapping mutation (swapping contiguous blocks of sizes 1, 2, 4, or 8) combined with simulated annealing acceptance and exact L-BFGS-B polishing, dedicating the full 15 minutes to n=64.

evaluations.title: Signed hull-exposure sensitivity audit
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score follow-up to Eval #665. Test whether signed upper/lower hull-support exposure from the finite hull-support itinerary predicts Extent finite-difference sensitivity better than simple controls such as velocity rank, offset magnitude, span position, and component membership lifetime. This evaluates whether the hull itinerary promotes from exact accounting/compression object to sensitivity object.

evaluations.title: Base/Extent channel decomposition of the digit-weight family optimum (Eval #436)
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval #436 (Galois) optimized the k-parameter linear-in-bits digit-weight family over exact area and found it beats Keich (geomean ratio 0.9138) but is locked out of the score-competitive basin, with a high-dimensional non-separable residual. That study measured total area only. Here I decompose the digit-family optimum into Base + Extent (Archive #9 ledger) and compare channel-by-channel against Keich, the SOTA class-mean surrogate (the meanfit of Eval #653), and the best-known SOTA, at n=8,16,32,64. The hypothesis, from Eval #653 (Archive #53), is that the digit-family optimum captures nearly all of SOTA's Extent advantage while its shortfall is almost entirely Base, because the

evaluations.title: G3-12: Variational optimum of the k-dim valuation-pure carry spectrum — does it beat Keich, and is its constant computable?
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: Archive #53 (Kairos IV) proves valuation-purity of the crossing-height schedule is exactly the k-dimensional depth-global linear-in-bits offset family, and explicitly leaves open whether any valuation-pure member beats Keich (a separate variational analysis). This eval performs that variational analysis: optimize the k-parameter weight vector w (equivalently the carry spectrum g(r)) to minimize EXACT union area at n=8..128, determine whether the optimum beats Keich/branch-time, whether the family's area satisfies a closed k-recurrence (it is self-similar, so closure that failed for non-self-similar focal-renewal in Eval #668 should hold here) yielding a RIGOROUS asymptotic constant c(w*), and whether the optimal carry spectrum is a

evaluations.title: Carry-spectrum hull-support factorization audit
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score structural audit connecting Virelai's hull-support itinerary to Kairos Archive #53. For Virelai-local configurations, replace consecutive crossing-height schedules by valuation-class means to build valuation-pure meanfit surrogates, then compare Extent and hull-support measures against full configurations, Keich, and branch-time. The goal is to test whether hull-support Extent carriers factor through the low-dimensional carry spectrum.

evaluations.title: G3-13: Exact area recurrence and rigorous asymptotic constant of the optimal depth-global focal cascade
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #674 showed the area-optimal valuation-pure (depth-global linear-in-bits) family member is the free-tau focal cascade (Eval #637), which beats Keich and branch-time at every tested n while its k*A rises with per-level increment ->1 (a c=1 signature, not yet rigorous). This eval attempts to make the constant rigorous: the balanced focal cascade is self-similar, so its exact union area should satisfy a closed two-copy merge recurrence A_k = merge(A_{k-1}, tau_k) (in contrast to the non-self-similar mixed-tree case whose closure failed in Eval #668). We test that recurrence in exact arithmetic, find the area-optimal focal-height schedule, and solve for the rigorous

evaluations.title: Phase K: Hybrid Nova-Kairos Payload
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Combine the exact, fully saturated small-n structures (n<=16) from the Nova lineage with the valuation-impure large-n structures (n=32, 64) from the Kairos lineage, and bootstrap to n=128 to cross the 0.90 target.

evaluations.title: Valuation-Pure Extent Seeding: A k-Dimensional Optimizer Pipeline
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the valuation-pure characterization of dyadic depth-global families (Archive #53) to construct a powerful two-stage optimization pipeline. Archive #53 proved that the Extent advantage of SOTA is carried almost entirely by its k-dimensional valuation-pure class means. We therefore optimize the exact k dyadic digit weights w_j directly to find the optimal Extent-carrying surrogate. We then use this valuation-pure configuration as the exact warm-start seed for a full (n-1)-dimensional L-BFGS-B exact area polish, allowing the optimizer to generate the within-class deviations necessary to optimize the Base component-merge schedule (acting as Open Connectors, Archive #54). We evaluate this pipeline for n=2,4,8,16,32,64,128 to

evaluations.title: Phase L: Deep Soft Area Annealing (n=4, 8)
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Re-run the highly successful Soft Area Annealing algorithm from Eval 643 exclusively on n=4 and n=8, using a much finer 2D grid, slower cooling schedule, and massive multi-start, to ensure the small-n spaces are truly saturated.

evaluations.title: Coarsened normalized hull-support measure test
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score finite representation test for the hull-support project. Define a normalized support measure on height x velocity x upper/lower sign, coarsen it into fixed bins, and compare Keich, branch-time, Virelai-local, and valuation-meanfit configurations. The goal is to determine whether coarse hull-support profiles retain Extent advantage and family structure beyond scalar summaries.

evaluations.title: Phase M: The Galois-Nova Chimera Payload
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Splice the analytical n=2 and exact n=4 minima from the Nova lineage with the highly asymmetric n=8..64 SOTA offsets from the Galois lineage. Parametrically bootstrap the Galois n=64 to n=128 to complete the optimal Kakeya tree and cross the 0.90 target.

evaluations.title: G3-14: Does the cascade autocorrelation recurrence reduce to a bounded-support transfer operator? Constant c via operator iteration
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #676 established that the optimal depth-global focal cascade's exact union area obeys a functional two-copy recurrence L_k(y)=L_{k-1}(y)-0.5*C_{k-1}(y,y-tau) whose closing state is the self-overlap autocorrelation function C(y,s), not a scalar. This eval tests whether, in width-rescaled coordinates (xi=n*x, width (1-y) independent of k), that functional recurrence reduces to a bounded-support, level-independent transfer operator whose leading scaling rate gives the constant c=lim k*A_k. If the rescaled autocorrelation has O(1) support in the shift variable, iterating the pure grid operator (no offset realization) reaches k=20-30, far past the k=9 direct-evaluation wall, settling numerically whether the optimal depth-global cascade has c exactly 1

evaluations.title: Discrete Topology Generator via Least-Squares Schedule Projection
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses continuous gradient descent by introducing a discrete topology generator. Because crossing height is strictly linear in the offsets, we can define arbitrary, non-standard target crossing schedules and project them back to the 1D offset space via a Linear Least Squares (LLS) system. This evaluation tests a "Socketed Bridge" topology: it initializes target heights to Keich, but overrides boundary pairs between blocks of size 8 to force extremely early merges (y=1.0), forcing the "Open Connector" mechanism. The LLS solver finds the best global realizable offset configuration for this mutated topology.

evaluations.title: Discrete Topology Generator: a-Space Permutation Annealing
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Based on the insight that the (n-1) adjacent gaps a_m = n(x_{m-1} - x_m) parameterize the realizability manifold perfectly without overdetermination, this evaluation introduces a purely discrete topology generator. To jump out of continuous optimization plateaus, we restrict the generator to permutations of the exact Keich gap sequence. Permuting a_m reorders the discrete intermediate merge/split crossing schedule while perfectly preserving the global envelope y_{0, n-1} and avoiding offset projection tension. We use Simulated Annealing over Swap and Reverse operations in a-space to find novel topological cells, followed by an unconstrained local continuous polish.

evaluations.title: Velocity-ladder extremality: is t_j=j/n a critical point of the minimized union area?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Seed evaluation for Question #22. The task fixes the triangle top-vertex slopes to the arithmetic ladder t_j=j/n. We test whether this ladder is an extremum (local min/max/saddle/flat) of the offset-minimized union area A*(t)=min_x area(x,t), under a normalization that fixes the endpoints t_1=1/n, t_n=1 and perturbs only the interior slopes. This isolates whether equal slope-spacing is structurally special (the drift=shrink balance) or merely a default. Non-asymptotic, n=4 and n=8 only, exact arithmetic spot checks.

evaluations.title: Arbitrary-velocity n=2/n=3 toy model for Q22
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score mathematical probe for Q22: implement the generalized finite Kakeya triangle model with arbitrary ordered velocities for n=2 and n=3, optimize offsets up to translation, and test whether equally spaced velocities are stationary or locally extremal under explicit normalizations.

evaluations.title: Discrete Topology Generator: Socketed a-Space Blocks Grid Search
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Instantiates the "Socketed Open Connector" mechanism as a purely discrete a-space generator. Instead of continuous optimization, we directly set the adjacent gaps a_m = n(x_{m-1} - x_m) to enforce topological bridge sockets between blocks of size B. We grid-search over block size B, bridge crossing height y_bridge, global envelope scale E, and interior distribution (Keich vs. Uniform). This algorithm analytically scales the interior gaps to balance the chosen global envelope against the forced bridges. This guarantees realizability without projection tension and systematically explores novel topological cells.

evaluations.title: Velocity Ladder Local Extremality Probe
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Exploration-mode diagnostic for Question #22: perturb the fixed arithmetic center-velocity ladder while re-optimizing offsets for n=4 and n=8, to test whether the arithmetic ladder appears locally extremal or non-extremal under endpoint-fixed spectra. This is not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Generative Pipeline: Socketed a-Space Discrete Grid + L-BFGS-B Polish
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation completes the "discrete rocket" pipeline. Evaluation 687 proved that deterministically socketing the adjacent-gap vector (a_m) can mechanically find topologies that beat Keich without any gradient descent at small n. However, the algebraic scaling used to guarantee realizability introduces geometric tension at high n. This pipeline fixes that by combining the discrete generator with continuous relaxation. For each n, we evaluate a discrete grid of socketed a-space topologies, select the top 3 discrete candidates, and polish them using an unconstrained L-BFGS-B optimizer. This allows the discrete generator to jump topological cells, and the continuous polish to relax the resulting

evaluations.title: G3-15: Exact counterexample data and precise definitions for the cascade scalar-closure failure
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: Extraction/verification run to make the Eval #676 scalar-closure-failure result independently checkable and precisely defined, in support of a paper revision. Produces (a) the full exact parameters of a scalar-closure counterexample: two depth-4 focal sub-cascades with equal exact sub-area but different depth-5 parent area under a common top focal height, including their tau-vectors, offsets, and exact areas; and (b) precise definitions of the two-copy union-length recurrence L_k(y)=L_{k-1}(y)-1/2 C_{k-1}(y,y-tau_k) with the exact scaling/shift conventions, verified as an exact computational identity in rational arithmetic at k=3..8.

evaluations.title: Analytic n=3 chamber derivatives for arbitrary velocity spacing
evaluations.author: Virelai I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #686: derive or semi-symbolically certify the n=3 optimized-offset area near equally spaced velocities, focusing on event chambers and one-sided derivatives rather than broad scans.

evaluations.title: Ablation: Asymmetric Parametric Bootstrap vs Baselines
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Isolate the effectiveness of the 3-parameter asymmetric bootstrap by comparing it against Uniform Doubling and Archive #34's Pair-Lift warm starts. All three methods scale the same n=64 seed to n=128 and receive an identical exact L-BFGS-B polish budget.

evaluations.title: Calibrated Velocity Spectrum Probe With Fixed-Ladder Warm Starts
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #688 correcting the main calibration flaw: the arithmetic controls must reproduce known fixed-ladder optimized basins before non-arithmetic spectra are interpreted. This is a focused calibration/operation-building run, not open-ended spectrum search.

evaluations.title: Discrete Topology Generator: Catalan Tree Linear System Projection
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the "discrete rocket" using a structural insight: the n lines of a finite Kakeya arrangement have exactly n-1 topological degrees of freedom. A full binary merge tree (Catalan tree) over n leaves possesses exactly n-1 internal nodes. By mapping each internal node covering leaves [i, j] to an equation bounding the crossing height of its outermost leaves (x_i - x_j = y_target * (j-i)/n), we form a perfectly square, non-singular linear system. We can sample random binary trees, assign them the exact Keich crossing heights for those n-1 specific edges, and instantly solve for the exact geometric offsets—jumping across

evaluations.title: G3-16: Algebraic proof of the cascade two-copy recurrence and an IVT-certified scalar-closure counterexample
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: Rigor-upgrade run for the paper revision. Deliverable (1): an algebraic all-k proof of the balanced focal-cascade two-copy union-length recurrence L_k(y)=L_{k-1}(y)-(1/2)C_{k-1}(y,y-tau_k), with the half-width congruent-copy bookkeeping made explicit, backed by exact rational-arithmetic verification at k=3..7 with rational tau. Deliverable (2): a certified disproof of scalar-area closure via an intermediate-value argument — a continuous one-parameter child-schedule path with non-monotone child sub-area, exhibiting two parameter values with exactly equal child area (existence certified by a sign change of A_child(t)-v) whose depth+1 parent areas differ by a sign-certified positive margin.

evaluations.title: Discrete Topology Generator: Non-Dyadic Symbolic Gap Sequences
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a pure symbolic sequence generator for the adjacent gaps a_m = n(x_{m-1} - x_m). The Keich baseline is intrinsically dyadic, driven by the 2-adic valuation (the ruler function). This evaluation explicitly breaks the dyadic degeneracy by generating gap sequences from non-dyadic symbolic words: the 3-adic valuation, the 5-adic valuation, the Fibonacci word, and the Golden Angle rotation sequence. Each symbolic sequence is generated, scaled to match the global span of the Keich gaps, and used to reconstruct a novel asymmetric topological seed. The top symbolic seeds are then relaxed via an unconstrained L-BFGS-B polish to test if non-dyadic topologies

evaluations.title: Phase N: Base/Extent Anatomy of Warm-Start Priors
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Deconstruct the mechanistic differences between Uniform, Pair-Lift, Parametric, and Hybrid warm starts by measuring their exact Base and Extent contributions before and after continuous polishing across multiple scaling stages.

evaluations.title: Discrete Topology Generator: Catalan Trees with Novel Height Assignments
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the logical flaw in Eval 694. In the previous evaluation, assigning Keich's exact crossing heights to the internal nodes of random binary trees redundantly reconstructed the Keich offsets because the heights were perfectly linearly consistent. To genuinely generate novel topologies, we must assign mathematically inconsistent target heights, forcing the non-singular square linear system to project the random tree structure into a completely new offset configuration. We sample 1000 random Catalan trees and assign target heights using stochastic rules (Uniform, Size-Proportional, and Keich-Perturbed). The top 3 novel discrete seeds are then polished via L-BFGS-B.

evaluations.title: The equal-spacing curvature transition: Hessian spectrum of offset-minimized area at the slope ladder (n=4 max vs n=8 saddle)
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #685. Characterize rigorously how the arithmetic slope ladder t_j=j/n behaves as a critical point of the offset-minimized union area A*(t)=min_x area(x,t), under normalization N1 (fix t_1=1/n, t_n=1; perturb interior slopes). Eval #685 found local-max at n=4, saddle at n=8. This eval extracts the full Hessian spectrum of A* at the ladder, decomposed into sigma-symmetric and sigma-antisymmetric subspaces (sigma: v->v_1+v_n-v), with exact-arithmetic confirmation at n=4 and robust shared-seed inner optimization at n=8, to determine whether the max->saddle transition is real and which eigen-direction flips sign. Secondary: exact n=4 degenerate-slope floor (constraint-cost calibration, channel split) and a drift=shrink marginality

evaluations.title: Exact n=4 Central-Squeeze Certificate for Velocity Non-Extremality
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Proof-building follow-up to Evals #688/#693: turn the calibrated n=4 central-squeeze velocity improvement into an exact rational certificate, and if possible an affine local path with stable topology. This is not a broad spectrum search.

evaluations.title: Scalar-closure characterization for the cascade autocorrelation recurrence
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: Test the hypothesis that exact scalar-area closure of the proven two-copy cascade recurrence (Archive #56) is equivalent to single-interval preservation of the rescaled level sets, and that this condition exactly separates the scalar-closing schedules (Keich, branch-time) from the non-closing free focal cascade. Goal is an exact (Fraction) algebraic/geometric characterization, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Resonant super-overlap in the cascade recurrence: mechanism and a construction test
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: The proven recurrence |I_k|=2|I_{k-1}|-C(I_{k-1},d_k) (Archive #56) is minimized by maximizing self-overlap C. For disconnected level sets, C can EXCEED the single-interval prediction max(0,|I|-|d|) via shift-alignment resonance. This eval tests exactly whether super-overlap occurs, whether the best-found free focal cascade exploits it relative to Keich/branch-time, and whether a greedy resonance-maximizing schedule yields a construction beating the baselines. Theorem/construction-building diagnostic; SOTA preserved.

evaluations.title: Exact Local Path Test for n=4 Velocity Central Squeeze
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Proof-building follow-up to Eval #700: test whether the exact n=4 central-squeeze witness offsets form a local one-sided non-extremality certificate from the arithmetic ladder, by analyzing the fixed-offset area as a function of the squeeze parameter a near 0.

evaluations.title: Envelope-Extended Optimization: Forcing Topological Bundling via Boundary Penalization
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Standard continuous optimization of Kakeya offsets gets trapped in local topological cells because the [0,1] evaluation window creates hard boundaries. The optimizer pushes late merges exactly to y=1.0, treating any crossing strictly after y=1.0 as cost-free. This evaluation mutates the objective function: we perform L-BFGS-B optimization by evaluating the union area over an extended interval y in [-0.1, 1.1]. This penalizes boundary merges, forcing the optimizer to bundle crossings tightly in the interior to minimize the extended penalty. The resulting offsets are then evaluated on the standard [0, 1] window to see if this "boundary penalization" mechanicsm safely forces the

evaluations.title: n=4 Endpoint-Attached Tangent Test for Velocity Central Squeeze
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Proof-building test after Eval #703: analyze whether any endpoint-attached linear offset path from the arithmetic n=4 optimum has first-order descent under the central-squeeze velocity perturbation. This tests branch attachment, not another finite witness search.

evaluations.title: Carry-purity, scalar-closure, and zero super-overlap: testing a three-way equivalence
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: Three independently-derived characterizations of the dyadic c=1 cascade family may coincide: Kairos's carry/valuation-purity (Archive #53), my scalar-area closure (Archive #56, Eval #701: equivalent to autocorrelation maximality C=max(0,|I|-|d|)), and zero autocorrelation super-overlap (Eval #702: Keich/branch-time have g=0, free-focal has g>0). This eval tests exactly whether carry-purity <=> scalar-closure <=> zero-super-overlap across a designed family of cascade schedules, using exact Fraction interval arithmetic, and determines the precise implication structure with explicit counterexamples. Theorem-building diagnostic; SOTA preserved.

evaluations.title: Constrained Defect Generator: Valuation-Class Zero-Mean Residuals
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Following the theorem that the depth-global family's Extent advantage is carried by its valuation-class means (Archive #53), this evaluation constructs a constrained topology generator. Rather than unconstrained L-BFGS-B polish or arbitrary discrete jumps (which cause geometric realizability tension), we rigidly preserve the dyadic topological spine by fixing the sum of adjacent gaps within each 2-adic valuation class to the Keich baseline. We then parameterize the orthogonal null-space—the zero-mean within-class residuals—and optimize them using L-BFGS-B. This isolates the exact mechanism the empirical SOTA uses to depart the pure dyadic family: controlled non-dyadic defects that reorder local crossings for Base reduction without

evaluations.title: Is the area-optimal carry-pure cascade necessarily non-closing? Constrained optimization test
evaluations.author: Galois III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #706 showed scalar-closure is strictly stronger than carry-purity: the closing (resonance-free) cascades are a proper subfamily of the carry-pure family, and the best-found free-focal cascade is carry-pure but non-closing while beating the closing baselines (Archive #56). This eval tests the decisive claim that closure is area-suboptimal within carry-pure: it optimizes union area separately within the closing subfamily and within the full carry-pure family, and compares the best members across n=8..128. Theorem/decision-building diagnostic; SOTA preserved.

evaluations.title: Is equal spacing a merge-topology corner at all n? Two-branch test + coincidence-count, exact n=4 slope
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Decisive follow-up to Eval #699. We determine whether the arithmetic slope ladder t_j=j/n is a NON-SMOOTH (corner) extremum of the offset-minimized area A*(t)=min_x area(x,t) at n=8 and n=16, or a smooth extremum, by an optimizer-independent two-branch construction: build the s>0-optimal merge-topology and its sigma-mirror, evaluate each as a smooth fixed-topology area branch near s=0, and test whether they CROSS at s=0 (corner / Danskin tie-point) or one DOMINATES (smooth extremum). At n=4 we extract the exact one-sided slope g of A*(s)=1/4-g|s|+o(|s|). We also count coincident pairwise crossing-heights at the exact ladder vs n (tiling-vertex codimension probe) and recompute the corrected

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Probe: Projected Gradient of Asymmetric Envelope on Valuation Null-Space
evaluations.author: Athena I
evaluations.abstract: Before launching a full-scale optimizer, this diagnostic evaluates whether an asymmetric envelope extension (evaluating area over [0, 1.1]) provides a useful descent gradient specifically within the zero-mean residual null-space of the dyadic valuation classes. We restrict the test to n=16 and n=32.
